jobs.title: Project Manager - Ft. Lauderdale - Remote
jobs.description:
At SSR, we’re more than a leading engineering design, consulting, and planning firm—we’re a team of owners committed to solving complex projects and delivering innovative solutions for facility and infrastructure challenges. With locations across the U.S. and expertise spanning diverse markets and services, our collaborative approach empowers us to build lasting partnerships with each other, our clients, and our communities.

We believe high performance and a people-first culture go hand in hand. As an owner from day one, our colleagues thrive in an environment that values accountability, celebrates achievement, and supports personal and professional growth. As owners, we take pride in our work and in each other—driving results while fostering a workplace where everyone feels seen, supported, and inspired.

Want to hear directly from our team? Visit http://www.ssr-inc.com/life-at-ssr and explore our culture on LinkedIn and Instagram.

What You’ll Do

As a Project Manager II, you will hold overall responsibility for medium to high complexity projects or multiple concurrent projects—leading teams to achieve Total Project Success by meeting scope, schedule, budget, and quality goals. You will serve as the primary client contact, coordinate multi‑discipline resources and subconsultants, manage financial performance, and ensure projects are executed according to plan from kickoff through close‑out. Every colleague has a voice and a stake in our success through our ESOP, and we are driven by our mission to make a positive difference for our clients, colleagues, and communities.

Confirm project scope and requirements with clients and stakeholders; document assumptions and decisions.
Develop proposals and financial plans; prepare preliminary man‑hour budgets with CRM, Department Head, or Operations Director.
Ensure contracts are fully executed by the appropriate Principal and align the team to contractual obligations.
Lead effective project kick‑offs to convey scope, standards, budgets, roles, risks, and expectations.
Finalize discipline work plans and task‑hour budgets with design leads; update plans as conditions change.
Establish schedules with client input; set interim milestones for timely information flow and coordination.
Schedule and sequence work; communicate action items; monitor manpower plans across disciplines and maintain profit variance within targets.
Maintain complete project documentation and organized storage; keep logs current (RFI, submittal, decision, risk).
Facilitate meetings with owners, clients, architects, and contractors; document decisions and follow‑ups.
Track budgets, fee burn, and earned value; recognize how hours charged impact revenue and forecasts.
Identify, negotiate, and administer fees for additional services; process change orders promptly.
Prepare and implement proactive QA/QC plans; coordinate timely reviews and submittals to meet standards and contract requirements.
Manage Construction Administration to help ensure installed systems conform to design intent and quality standards.
Ensure accurate invoices are issued promptly; track AR status and update projected monthly revenue.
Resolve design and coordination issues by analyzing root causes and driving cross‑discipline solutions.
Supervise close‑out activities including punchlists, documentation, filings, lessons learned, and archive.
Build and grow client relationships through exceptional delivery; engage in business development with current and potential clients to expand services.

Minimum Requirements

Who We’re Looking For

Technical or Bachelor’s degree in one of the major technical disciplines practiced by the firm with eight years related project experience OR
Twelve years of practical experience on similar projects
Demonstrated, consistent ability to manage projects of various size and complexity
Professional Engineer Licensure preferred (required by those who have a ABET accredited degree in engineering)

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading multi‑discipline design teams and coordinating subconsultants and contractors.
Command of project financials including pricing, fee burn, earned value, forecasts, and AR.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and comfort with scheduling and resource planning tools.
Clear, concise communication and meeting facilitation; strong documentation and follow‑through.
Ability to analyze issues, evaluate trade‑offs, mitigate risk, and make sound decisions in collaboration with stakeholders.
Business development mindset with experience supporting proposals, interviews, and client workshops.

What We Offer

100% Employee-Owned – Ownership from day one with immediate ESOP vesting.
Retirement Savings – 401(k) with immediate vesting and a generous company match.
Health & Wellness – Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus company‑funded HSA contributions for HDHP plans.
Company-Paid Protection – Life insurance, AD&D, and short and long term disability at no cost to you.
Work-Life Balance – Flexible schedules, paid parental leave, generous PTO, and paid company holidays.
Career Growth – Tuition reimbursement and ongoing professional development support.

SSR is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action Employer

EEO Disabled/Veterans

Project Tracking & Reporting – Monitor project status, track technical issues, and provide clear and effective reporting on milestones, deliverables, expectations, dependencies, risks, mitigation plans, escalations, and overall progress.
Coaching and support project team to follow PMO processes and procedures to support on time, quality, and scope goals.
Stakeholder Communication & Issue Management – Facilitate communication with internal and external stakeholders, addressing project-related concerns and ensuring alignment on integration and deployment efforts.
Program Governance & Best Practices – Drive program integrity and coherence by maintaining an effective environment within PMO, establishing program-related practices, templates, policies, tools, and partnerships to improve organizational capabilities.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Natural Gas Projects
jobs.description:
We’re a team of friends bound together by a mission to preserve our planet for future generations through innovative energy solutions and modern infrastructure. Intersect develops, constructs, and operates the most ambitious power and data center infrastructure in the country by co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation.

Intersect was acquired by Google in March 2026 and operates as an independent subsidiary. We are developing and constructing multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects in the U.S., enabling more data center and generation capacity to come online faster. We’re on an aggressive growth trajectory and looking for people hungry to tackle the largest energy challenges on the planet.

Location & Team Gatherings

Intersect has been a fully flexible workplace since its founding in 2016.  We’ve been very intentional about the way we do things. We are not work-from-home, hybrid, or in-office - we are any and all of those options! Deepening social connections and offering shared experiences is a cornerstone of the way we work. We connect as a team at our Team Week experiences four times a year and at our recently established Hub locations - SF Bay Area, NYC Metro Area, NY; Denver, CO; Austin, TX; Calgary, AB; and Toronto, ON.

We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.

About this role

As a Project Manager - Natural Gas Projects on Intersect's Datacenters and Fuels / Natural Gas Power Projects team, you'll lead the execution of critical power generation and energy infrastructure projects at the convergence of electrification, digitalization, and decarbonization. Acting as the owner's representative across the project lifecycle, you'll guide complex natural gas-fired facilities—including reciprocating engine plants, gas turbine facilities, HV switchyards, substations, BESS, and large-scale data center power infrastructure—from development through commissioning and commercial operation.

Engineering oversight and technical judgment are central to this position. You will apply engineering principles to review technical designs, evaluate equipment and EPC contractor proposals, and resolve complex field and design issues while driving safety, quality, schedule, and budget performance.

Team overview

This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect's mission to accelerate the clean energy transition by delivering reliable, dispatchable power infrastructure that supports large-scale digital and electrical loads. The Datacenters and Fuels / Natural Gas Power Projects team partners across engineering, construction, commercial, and operations to execute resilient generation assets from initial design through commercial handover. Joining this group means taking direct ownership of high-impact infrastructure projects and growing alongside seasoned technical leaders committed to operational excellence.

What you'll do

Lead Complex Project Execution and Controls

Develop and execute comprehensive project plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and risk registers for natural gas-fired power generation facilities from development through commercial operation and turnover.

Drive project performance against safety, quality, schedule, budget, and operational readiness objectives while providing clear, actionable updates to executive leadership.

Lead risk identification, mitigation planning, project closeout activities, and commissioning support to ensure seamless handover to operations teams.

Manage EPC and External Partner Performance

Serve as the primary owner's representative for EPC contractors, consultants, utilities, and equipment vendors across all project phases.

Oversee contractor compliance, commercial negotiations, change orders, and claims resolution, including rigorous technical evaluation of contractor proposals.

Review and approve construction strategies, procurement plans, and execution methodologies while maintaining productive alignment across stakeholder groups.

Deliver Technical and Engineering Excellence

Partner with engineering teams to review and approve technical designs, vendor submittals, and construction approaches, guiding decisions on design basis, equipment selection, and technical scope.

Oversee the integration of reciprocating engine plants, gas turbine facilities, HV switchyards and substations, BESS assets, and large-scale data center power infrastructure.

Drive QA/QC processes, technical bid evaluations, equipment performance guarantees, and startup/commissioning test procedures across engineering, procurement, and construction.

Champion Safety, Compliance, and Cross-Functional Alignment

Foster a culture of safety excellence by conducting site inspections, field reviews, and audits to verify adherence to safety management systems, environmental permits, and federal, state, and local regulations.

Partner closely with internal engineering, construction, commercial, and operations teams to resolve technical challenges, maintain project momentum, and build long-run value.

What you'll bring

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or a related engineering discipline (Required).

10+ years of progressive experience in project execution, construction management, or engineering leadership within power generation, energy infrastructure, oil & gas, utility, or heavy industrial sectors.

Direct experience executing natural gas-fired power generation projects (reciprocating engine plants or gas turbine facilities) from either the Owner's or EPC Contractor's side through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

Strong technical grounding in HV switchyards, substations, BESS integration, and large-scale power infrastructure, with proven ability to evaluate technical designs, equipment proposals, and change orders.

Working knowledge of QA/QC frameworks, commissioning and startup test procedures, and safety management systems.

A hands-on leadership style that emphasizes face-to-face collaboration, composure under competing priorities, and disciplined commercial and technical negotiation.

A commitment to collaboration, continuous learning, inclusion, and long-term value creation aligned with Intersect's values of Equity, Humility, Authenticity, Long-run Value, and People Come First.

Total Rewards

Total Compensation:
$188,500 - $205,400 (total compensation includes base salary + bonus in USD)

Equity:
Beyond your salary, you’ll receive an Equity Grant, giving you a meaningful stake in our parent company. 

Health & wellness:
100% premium coverage for you and your dependents on medical, dental, and vision

Time to recharge:
Unlimited PTO, plus two company-wide breaks (Fourth of July & end of year)

Family support:
Up to 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, plus 6 additional weeks for birth parents; access to family planning and family care support through Carrot and Maven

Mental health:
Free access to Spring Health, including 5 free therapy and psychiatry sessions, plus a Headspace account for mindfulness and meditation through our physical health vendor, Wellhub+

Perks & extras:
$150 monthly food stipend, $150 monthly reimbursement for cell phone and internet, pet insurance allowance, full home office setup, free access to UrbanSitter with $625 in quarterly company-paid credits, ActiveHero, and One Medical

jobs.title: Interdisciplinary AI Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Title: 
Interdisciplinary AI Project Manager
Job Status: 
Full-time, 18-month term (with projected extension), grant-funded position 
Reports to: 
Senior Manager of Standards
Location: 
Fully Remote 
Salary Range: 
$80,000 – $85,000 annually
The Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA) is a membership organization that supports and promotes the teaching of computer science, providing opportunities for PK-12 teachers and their students to better understand computer science and to more successfully prepare themselves to teach and learn. 
CSTA is looking for an experienced Project Manager who will lead the implementation of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative, a national effort to bring computer science and other disciplines together to define and teach AI literacy across PK–12 education
. The Project Manager will coordinate convenings of national subject-area associations, manage the development of interdisciplinary instructional resources with CS and non-CS educators, guide dissemination and professional development aligned to these resources, and work with contractors and external reviewers to ensure all project deliverables are met, and advocate for adoption of the project's outputs across the education community. 
Project Description AI literacy can't be the responsibility of computer science alone. Students encounter AI in every subject, and each discipline has a distinct role in helping them understand, use, and critically evaluate it. The purpose of the Collaborative is to define that shared responsibility and give educators the tools to act on it.
CSTA is convening national subject-area associations, including those representing mathematics, English language arts, science, world languages, and technology and engineering into a cross-subject collaborative. Through three convenings, the collaborative will produce an interdisciplinary AI Literacies Framework and a Division-of-Labor Map describing how responsibility for AI literacy is distributed across subject areas. Both will be publicly launched at the CSTA Annual Conference in July 2027.
Alongside this work, the Collaborative brings CS and non-CS educators together in collaborative workshops to develop, classroom-test, and refine interdisciplinary instructional resources that integrate foundational AI concepts with subjects such as math, ELA, and social studies. The resources are aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards and other disciplinary standards. Together, these efforts will shape how AI literacy is taught across disciplines in schools nationwide. 
Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesFramework Development (30%) Contribute to the planning and facilitation of three cross-disciplinary convenings
to create an interdisciplinary AI literacy framework and division of labor map.

Synthesize convening and project outcomes and recommendations and publish supporting materials in report(s)
, in close collaboration with a contracted Report Writer, a contracted Designer, CSTA staff, and external reviewers.

Interdisciplinary Resource Development (30%) Refine and manage processes to develop, publish, and disseminate interdisciplinary instructional resources aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Standards and other disciplinary standards (e.g., Next Generation Science Standards, Common Core State Standards for Mathematics/ELA).

Recruit
representatives for collaborative, interdisciplinary instructional resource development.

Plan and facilitate
interdisciplinary instructional resource development workshops.

Facilitate
the development of interdisciplinary professional learning opportunities.

Project Management and Dissemination (40%) Manage the successful implementation
of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative project. Success includes the development and publication of an interdisciplinary framework for AI education and division-of-labor map, and the development and publication of interdisciplinary lesson plans across several subject areas.

Maintain the public-facing display
of developed resources.

Coordinate with external reviewers
and other contractors
to ensure needed feedback and timely delivery of project deliverables.

Work closely with CSTA staff to create and manage reporting
to sponsor(s) and other key audiences, including developing cross-subject case studies. 

Guide dissemination
and professional development
(PD) efforts aligned with the project's interdisciplinary resources and outputs.

Present
externally on the project across multiple audiences at regular intervals (6–12 times per year, domestically and virtually), and advocate
for adoption of the framework, division of labor map, and interdisciplinary instructional resources.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience & Qualifications You will be successful in this role if you have:
Demonstrated strong project management and organizational skills, including workflow management, coordinating a variety of tasks simultaneously, and attention to detail

Superior critical thinking skills and judgment, with an ability to maintain a professional, upbeat attitude

Demonstrated partner management experience, working with external stakeholders and delivering quality customer service and ability to continuously improve methods and procedures

A bachelors or masters degree in education, instructional design, computer science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience

Experience with PK-12 curriculum development 

Familiarity with AI in PK-12 education, including foundational AI concepts and current AI literacy efforts

Experience in planning and facilitating meetings with clear objectives, agendas, and collaborative structures

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially on virtual interfaces; comfort with speaking to groups and presenting information

Comfort with working in a remote environment; proficiency in working with technology – including but not limited to Google Workspace, videoconferencing (e.g., Zoom), project management software (e.g., Asana), and electronic communications (e.g., Slack)

Commitment to engaging in CSTA's efforts towards embracing diversity, being purposefully inclusive, and addressing anti-racism in CS education

The ability to travel up to 15% of the time (all travel costs are covered by CSTA)

The ability and willingness to shift work schedule to support or manage professional learning in afternoons, evenings, and weekends to accommodate teacher participants

Preferred Qualifications Experience teaching PK-12 computer science and/or AI literacy skills

Experience with interdisciplinary or cross-curricular teaching or curriculum design, particularly integrating computing into other subject areas

Experience working with national education organizations, coalitions, or multi-organization partnerships

Experience as a CSTA volunteer, committee member, chapter leader, or similar leadership role in an organization for PK-12 teachers

Position Terms This is a grant-funded position termed for 18-months. Position extension is planned but contingent on funding and approval by the CSTA Executive Director. CSTA is unable to sponsor employment visas. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a pre-employment background check and verification of eligibility to work in the United States.
Benefits Benefits of working at CSTA include:
Flexible, engaging remote working environment with a great team

Unlimited flexible paid time off policy including one week office closures twice annually in July/August and at the end of December

Paid parental leave of eight to twelve weeks

Medical, dental and vision premiums paid at 100% for FT positions and subsidized dependent premiums

Technology subsidy consistent with our Bring Your Own Device environment

Option to participate in a retirement savings plan with employer match after six months

Application process Please submit a cover letter and two-page resume. Please submit application directly on the original job posting site: 
https://csta.prismhr-hire.com/job/1069920/interdisciplinary-ai-project-manager
The application process will consist of a brief screening interview, a panel interview, and potentially a final round interview, all conducted virtually.
Preference will be given to applications submitted by November 8, 2026.

CSTA values building a diverse workplace and community. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need, and all qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. Applicants from historically underrepresented communities in computing, including but not limited to people of color, LGBTQ individuals, and women, are strongly encouraged to apply.

We make digital transformation a reality by leveraging AI, Enterprise Performance Management (EPM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Supply Chain Management (SCM), Human Capital Management (HCM), Customer Experience (CX), Analytics, and Data Management for the cloud. Through connected capabilities, we bring people, processes, and technology together. We help organizations go further faster. That is the Peloton way!
What truly sets us apart is our people. We are team players. We are energetic and entrepreneurial. We are problem solvers and innovative thinkers who believe the best outcomes are built together. Title: eHealth Exchange Onboarding Program Manager

Reports to: eHealth Exchange Director, Governance and Onboarding
FLSA Status: Exempt, Full Time
Supervisory Responsibility: N/A
Location: Remote
Starting Salary Range: $100,000 - 120,000 depending on experience

POSITION SUMMARY:
The eHealth Exchange Onboarding Program Manager helps to drive the success of the eHealth Exchange, a health IT "network of networks" with nationwide scope, through a range of customer implementations as it relates to onboarding, testing, and technical support. The Program Manager guides health systems, ambulatory providers, HIEs, and other new customers as they initially connect to the eHealth Exchange network and to address onboarding requirements including ensuring the appropriate documentation is in place, basic technical troubleshooting, and testing. The Program Manager also helps identify new eHealth Exchange services and assists current customers with onboarding to those new services.
The role involves some independent work, with responsibility for administering best practices for designing and implementing plans according to customer requirements. The role is highly visible and customer facing with the expectation that each customer is provided with the highest quality customer service and exceptional communication to ensure flawless execution during their implementation and support.
The Program Manager will contribute to the development, improvement, and documentation of implementation processes these organizations follow as part of their participation in interoperable exchange.
This position requires a blend of project management, process knowledge, product knowledge, technical knowledge (IHE / FHIR), and strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills, and an eager willingness to learn—as it relates to the ever-evolving policy & technical healthcare landscape.

Who is eHealth Exchange?
The eHealth Exchange supports operational health information exchange activities, with services ranging from legal and policy governance, to identification of standards, and technical directory and security components.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
Interact directly and independently with customers (ranging from small to large national organizations and governmental agencies) through each phase of the eHealth Exchange onboarding process from the initial inquiry, application, testing, and through activation.
Prepare detailed and accurate implementation status reports and work proactively to resolve gaps and issues and keep the implementation on track.
Educate potential applicants on how to join eHealth Exchange along with the testing requirements and highlight the benefits of the applicable eHealth Exchange use cases.
Encourage current eHealth Exchange customers to adopt new eHealth Exchange services and use cases.
Facilitate calls with federal agencies to communicate and coordinate the status of outreach and onboarding activities.
Guide applicants and participants to the appropriate technical standards, directory entry file, specifications, testing resources, and assist in policy inquiries where necessary.
Develop, maintain and manage technical onboarding plans inclusive to pre-requisite requirements, testing, technical validation, and production activation.
Maintain customer records such as contacts and services deployed.
Create annual contracts and supply Accounting with the necessary information to generate invoices. Update contracts with invoicing and payment details supplied by Accounting.
Process legal agreements with customers and facilitate requested changes to legal documents.
Collaborate with all cross-functional internal team members and effectively maintain and build relationships across business groups while working in a highly consultative manner with the customer to ensure that the expectations are clearly defined.
Direct the production of requirements documents which communicate process workflow and data/functional/operational needs effectively and accurately to both business stakeholders and technical staff.
Anticipate customer needs and operational issues and proactively coordinate with customer and eHealth Exchange staff to overcome the obstacles and exceed the customer's expectations.
Provide enhancements and continuous process improvements.
Host the Monthly All Participant Call and ensure that there is a meaningful agenda (with qualified presenters) each month.
Respond to Administrator@ehealthexchange emails including coordinating introductory calls, triaging Applicant or Participant issues and answering questions within the required timeframe. Ensure coverage when out of the office.
Conduct applicant testing and submitting of messages in validation and production environments, coordinate with certificate sponsor.
Assist with other projects as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:
Operational knowledge of health IT interoperability transactions is highly preferred, particularly the overall workflow, technology and business process intersections.
Demonstrated technical capability combined with the ability to effectively communicate technical detail to non-technical individuals.
Exceptional consulting skills and customer savviness with proven ability to plan and work with customer through implementation process, while keeping efforts on track with milestones.
Strong project management skills with proven ability to independently and successfully apply process acumen to process improvement projects, with measurable business performance improvement outcomes.
Ability to multi-task in rapidly evolving environment, in condensed timeframes with demonstrated ability to work against a plan, meet deadlines and produce deliverables relative to target dates.
Strong problem solving and critical thinking skills with ability to identity and develop plans to mitigate issues from escalating and to identify creative solutions to avoid impeding implementation efforts.
Ability to work with a customer’s senior level management (typically Director / CIO) to provide updates and address escalated matters that affect the customer’s implementation timeframe.
Exceptional interpersonal skills and the ability to influence, negotiate, and lead regardless of title or authority.
Proven ability to influence complicated courses of action when others are directly accountable for outcomes.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent attention to detail and communications skills.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience

Consultant experience preferred
Business Associate Agreement contracting experience preferred
Experience with InterSystems HealthShare and IRIS for Health preferred

Ability to stand or sit for extended periods of time

Strong program management, risk management, and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines within a structured framework.

Self-starter, with strong business acumen and a customer-first mindset, capable of solving problems and building deep, meaningful relationships with customers and internal stakeholders.
Demonstrates a focus on process optimization, service enhancement, and driving customer success.
Passionate about learning, building solutions, and tackling challenges.
Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, with experience working across multi-cultural, cross-functional teams.

401K plan

And much, much more!

jobs.description:
Full-time Description

About Us

At Kroll Konstruction, we specialize in delivering complex projects with a focus on safety-first culture, quality, and collaboration. We are committed to the values of service, accountability, and doing whatever it takes to get the job done right.

Overview

The Project Manager role oversees commercial construction from setup to closeout, ensuring projects meet deadlines, stay within budget, and adhere to the highest safety and quality standards. This role requires strong leadership skills, excellent communication, and a hands-on approach to coordinating site activities, managing subcontractors, and upholding compliance with project requirements.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Budget & Compliance Oversight

Collaborate with Accounting and Senior Leadership to maintain accurate reporting on budget performance and financial forecasts.
Develop, manage, and maintain project budgets from pre-construction through closeout, ensuring all expenditures align with approved costs and contractual limits.
Review and approve subcontractor/vendor invoices, change orders, and purchase requests to ensure cost accuracy and adherence to budget limits.
Identify and reconcile variances between planned and actual costs, taking prompt corrective action to maintain budget.
Ensure project compliance with applicable codes, regulations, safety standards, and company policies.

Contract Management

Review prime contracts, subcontracts, and purchase orders to confirm scope, schedule, and terms are properly executed and communicated.
Lead negotiations of subcontractor agreements and change orders in collaboration with Senior Leadership and relevant teams.
Monitor and enforce contract compliance, ensuring all parties meet deliverables, insurance requirements, and performance obligations.
Manage project documentation, including RFIs, submittals, and contract correspondence, ensuring traceability and timely resolution.
Oversee project closeout documentation, including warranties, support with lien waivers, and final payment approvals.

Scheduling & Project Oversight

Develop and maintain the project schedule in coordination with the superintendent, subcontractors, and Owners, ensuring milestones are met.
Identify potential delays or resource conflicts and implement mitigation strategies immediately with Senior Leadership to maintain on-time delivery.
Lead weekly coordination meetings with field and office teams to review progress, resolve issues, and forecast upcoming activities.
Monitor quality, safety, and performance in collaboration with Operations teams.
Ensure all work aligns with project specifications, drawings, and company standards for workmanship and professionalism.

Metrics & Reporting

Track and report key project metrics, including budget performance, schedule adherence, safety incidents, and quality control findings.
Prepare and present regular project status updates to relevant stakeholders.
Analyze performance data, identify trends, and recommend process improvements for future projects (Lessons Learned).
Maintain accurate documentation within project management platforms (e.g., RedTeam, BIM 360, etc.) to ensure transparency and accountability.

Subcontractor Management

Conduct pre-construction and weekly coordination meetings with Owners, Superintendents, and Leadership to align expectations.
Foster strong partnerships, escalating performance or contractual issues to Senior Leadership when necessary, to ensure collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Evaluate and oversee subcontractor performance, ensuring quality, safety-first culture, and schedule compliance.
Verify scope completion and assist with the approval of progress billings and retainage release.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent field experience.
OSHA 30 certification required; PMP certification preferred.
Advanced knowledge of construction contracts and project management practices, and regulatory requirements.
5+ years of demonstrated experience in commercial construction management, preferably with a general contractor, from bid to closeout.

Technical & Leadership Skills:

Proficiency with online project management or scheduling tools (RedTeam, Bluebeam, MS Project).
Skilled in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
Ability to partner cross-functionally to ensure contract-aligned scheduling, budgeting, and subcontractor coordination.
Experience managing design-build or fast-track projects.
Strong understanding of job cost tracking and forecasting principles.
Ability to analyze data, interpret reports, and identify cost or scheduling trends.
Leadership style rooted in accountability, collaboration, and safety-first culture.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Field personnel on construction project teams should expect 60-hour workweeks, with a minimum of 5 days a week and 8 hours per day, including weekends. Travel home is typically every week, but can shift to every third week depending on project needs. During the final month and a half of a project, it's common to remain on-site and take extra time off after completion.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.

Fine motor skills: Regular use of hands for tasks like typing, using a mouse, and handling documents.
Repetitive motions: Frequent reaching and arm movements, particularly when using the phone and during meetings.
Occasional lifting: The ability to lift up to 25 pounds may be required occasionally, but it's not a primary job function.

Kroll Konstruction Offers

100% company-paid premium medical, dental, vision, life ($50,000), AD&D ($50,000), and long-term disability insurance for our employees.
10 Paid Personal Days Off (PTO) and 8 Paid Holidays.
Discretionary Performance Bonus: Up to 10% of base salary, contingent upon company profitability and at the company's sole discretion.

Important Details:

This is a hybrid travel position requiring 100% travel availability based on project assignments.
Project Managers are expected to travel nationwide to active job sites, with a minimum of one site visit per week. Additional travel may be required based on project needs, project milestones, incident response, or strategic business initiatives.
When not assigned to a project site, work may be performed remotely from a home office, from one of our office locations, or from another approved work location.
Candidates must be willing and able to travel extensively, including overnight travel, as required to support project execution.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Project Manager directs project staff and manages subcontractors to ensure effective coordination, strong performance, and adherence to safety and quality expectations.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Activities, duties, or responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Third-Party Recruiters

Kroll Konstruction does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies or search firms. Agencies should not contact hiring managers or other employees directly. All recruiting inquiries must be directed to the Human Resources Department. Resumes submitted without a current, signed vendor agreement will be considered the property of Kroll Konstruction, and no placement fee will be paid.

Salary Description $85,000.00- $115,000

Job Description

Help organisations build the tech skills they need, one successful delivery at a time. As a Project Manager, you own the course delivery process from start to finish. Your projects can be a single instructor-led class, a multi-course programme, a webinar, or an academy that upskills, reskills, or onboards a team over a defined period. Academies blend instructor-led learning, labs, self-paced courses, capstones, and Skill IQ assessments.

You will shape what’s next for clients by turning plans into programmes that work. You will grow with purpose, taking on work that ranges from a few weeks to a full year. And you will thrive together with Professional Services Account Executives, instructors, and internal teams who rely on you to keep delivery on track.

What You’ll Do

Own delivery from the signed statement of work through to sharing evaluation scores with the client, and meet every deadline along the way.
Measure success by client quality and satisfaction scores.
Manage client programmes that run from a few weeks to a full year, including weekly calls, quarterly business reviews, and learning plans and schedules.
Join pre-sale discovery calls and work with Account Executives to scope projects accurately and confirm the right instructors, technology, and resources are ready.
Work with clients and instructors to define tech setup needs and arrange cloud-based environments.
Manage project budgets and profitability, and build client relationships that inspire confidence in high-quality delivery.

What You’ll Bring

A talent for organising your workload and moving several projects forward at once
Skill in facilitation and conflict resolution that keeps clients, instructors, and teammates aligned
Clear communication with internal and external stakeholders, from sales teams to client leaders
A relationship-first approach that builds client trust over time
Comfort working with project budgets and tracking profitability
AI literacy (preferred, not required)

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of professional experience in project or programme management
4+ years of customer engagement or customer success experience
Travel: Travel expectations differ by role. Some quota-bearing sales positions involve limited travel, while others may involve travel of up to 40%, depending on business needs.
Hybrid Work Model: This role follows a hybrid schedule, with on-site work at our Dublin, Ireland office Wednesday and Thursday and remote flexibility on Mondays, Tuesdays and Fridays. This approach helps us collaborate more effectively, make decisions more quickly, and build a stronger culture, while still providing flexibility.

Why you’ll love working here

We work in a blended environment that supports collaboration, flexibility, and connection across teams.
We are mission-driven, shaping the future of tech upskilling and delivering impact that matters.
We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging, where everyone can contribute and thrive.
We are always learning, creating an environment where you can take on new challenges, expand your skills, and grow with purpose.
Benefits include competitive compensation, bonus eligibility, comprehensive medical coverage, unlimited PTO, wellness reimbursement, professional development funds, and more.

About Us

Exceptional written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

How You'll Help Us Keep Climbing (Overview & Key Responsibilities)

The DMS Program Manager is responsible for overseeing third-party vendors performing services on behalf of Delta Air Lines and Delta Material Services (DMS). These services include aircraft storage, reactivation, disassembly, engine preservation, maintenance execution, parts harvesting, inventory management, warehousing, and asset sales. The Program Manager serves as the primary liaison between Delta/DMS and external vendors, ensuring all activities are executed in compliance with FAA regulations, Delta policies, quality standards, operational requirements, and commercial objectives.

This role drives vendor accountability, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, cost control, schedule adherence, and continuous improvement across all assigned programs while maintaining the highest standards of safety and airworthiness.

Key Responsibilities - Vendor Oversight & Compliance

Direct oversight of vendor operations supporting aircraft storage, maintenance, engine preservation, disassembly, and parts harvesting activities.
Ensure vendor compliance with FAA regulations, Delta and DMS policies, procedures, quality standards, and airworthiness requirements.
Verify proper certification, documentation, and release of aircraft, engines, components, and materials.
Conduct routine audits and process reviews to validate procedural compliance and operational effectiveness.

Program Execution & Operational Management

Monitor daily vendor performance, project progress, and schedule adherence to support Delta and DMS operational requirements.
Communicate program status, risks, and deviations from plan to internal stakeholders and leadership.
Collaborate with vendors and cross-functional teams to resolve issues related to scope, quality, cost, schedule, and resource allocation.
Drive corrective actions and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance vendor performance and operational results.

Inventory & Materials Management

Ensure accurate inventory control throughout removal, tagging, transportation, warehousing, and distribution processes.
Validate vendor transactions within SAP, MIRS, and related systems to maintain material traceability and inventory accuracy.
Conduct random inspections of parts and components to verify serviceability and regulatory compliance prior to shipment.
Investigate inventory discrepancies, tagging errors, shipping issues, and removal damage events to determine root causes and implement sustainable solutions.

Financial & Commercial Oversight

Review and validate vendor invoices, work packages, and billed services to ensure alignment with contractual scope and completed work.
Monitor project costs and identify opportunities to optimize operational and financial performance.
Support strategic decision-making through analysis of vendor performance metrics, operational trends, and business impacts.

Training & Stakeholder Engagement

Coordinate and oversee vendor training on critical Delta and DMS processes, systems, and compliance requirements.
Monitor training completion and ongoing compliance with established standards.
Serve as the primary point of contact for vendor operations, fostering strong partnerships and driving accountability through collaboration and performance management.

What You Need To Succeed (Minimum Qualifications)

Consistently prioritizes safety and security of self, others, and personal data.
Embraces diverse people, thinking, and styles.
Possesses a high school diploma, GED, or high school equivalency.
Is at least 18 years of age and has authorization to work in the United States.
FAA Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) License required.
Minimum five years of aviation maintenance, engineering, technical operations, or aircraft asset management experience.
Extensive knowledge of aircraft systems, technical documentation, maintenance programs, airworthiness requirements, and regulatory compliance.
Strong understanding of aircraft storage, preservation, reactivation, disassembly, and parts harvesting processes.
Willingness to work off-shift hours, weekends, and holidays as operational demands require.
Ability to travel extensively (80%-100%) in support of vendor oversight and program execution.
Position is safety-sensitive and subject to applicable drug-testing requirements. Demonstrates and promotes Delta's core values of: Honesty, Integrity, Respect, Perseverance, Servant Leadership
Promote and maintain a strong safety culture by ensuring compliance with all safety policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrate safety-conscious behaviors in all operational activities and decision-making processes.

Working knowledge of Delta TechOps systems, including SCEPTRE, MIRS, GEM, SAP, and related operational platforms.
Experience with inventory control, materials management, and supply chain processes.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Access, and Project.

Experience leading process improvement initiatives and delivering measurable operational results.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to support the growth of the world's most innovative HealthCare data platform. InterSystems HealthShare is the engine behind some of the world's most critical health applications. We are the platform technology that empowers mission-critical solutions across health plans, providers, and public sector.

About The Role

This is a founding Technical Program Manager role for HealthShare. You will report to the Head of Product and stand up the TPM function for the platform, defining how it works from the ground up. You will own the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Quality Development, and the Release Team: the dependencies between them, the handoffs where one team's work becomes another's, and the readiness of the releases that span all four.

This is a role for someone who has built this foundational function before and understands the distinction that makes it work. Engineering owns delivery on its teams. Quality owns quality. The Release Team owns the release. The TPM owns the seams between them, the cross-team dependency graph, and the standard for how work is tracked and made visible, without taking on the work that belongs to those teams or drifting into collecting status on their behalf.

If you are energized by defining an operating model rather than inheriting one, and by making a fast-moving, technically deep organization legible to itself without slowing it down, this role is built for you.

What You'll Own

The seams between Product, Engineering, Quality Development, and the Release Team. Name the handoffs, assign an owner on each side, define what passes across each boundary, and set the escalation path for when something breaks, before the release that tests it.
The cross-team dependency graph. Maintain an explicit, current picture of what depends on what across teams, so the organization can make deliberate decisions about sequencing and risk instead of discovering a major dependency the week it blocks a release.
Launch and release readiness for cross-functional work that spans multiple teams. Know, before a date is committed, whether the engineering work, the quality gates, the release steps, and the downstream communication are going to converge.
The tracking standard in Jira and Confluence. Define how work is structured and made visible, so program state is readable directly, without a status meeting. Make the compliant path the easy path so teams follow it because it helps them, not because they are told to.
Risk identification and communication across the platform. Surface the cross-team risks the individual teams are too close to see and get them in front of the right people early, using Teams and the tools the organization already operates.
Program-level visibility for leadership. Give the Head of Product and senior stakeholders a legible read on program health that is a byproduct of how teams already work, not a separate reporting tax layered on top of them.

What We're Looking For

10+ years in technical program management or a closely related discipline, including experience standing up or scaling a program-management function, not only running programs within an existing one.
Strong technical fluency. You do not need to write production code, but you should read a system well enough to find the real risk in a plan and hold your own with senior engineers on dependencies and architecture.
Experience delivering managed services and cloud services, and comfort with the operational realities of both.
A clear, demonstrated point of view on the difference between technical program management and a PMO, and on why performing hygiene work on behalf of teams is a failure mode rather than a service.
A track record of building cross-functional processes and interfaces that held up under real delivery pressure, spanning engineering and the teams downstream of it.
Experience defining a tracking standard that many teams run on, in Jira, Confluence, or equivalent tooling.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You can make a technical program legible to an engineer and to an executive in the same day, and you can hold a position through clarity and judgment rather than positional authority.
Strong organizational instincts and attention to detail, balanced by the judgment to add the minimum process a problem actually requires.

Tools You'll Work With

Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft productivity applications.

optimizing spend.

As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.

Manager, Program Management (Community Connect)

Summary

HII - Mission Technologies seeking a highly qualified Program Manager (PM) to support the U.S. Department of State, Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs, Office of Aviation (INL/A). The PM will provide senior level leadership, strategic guidance, and management oversight for a large, complex, multi national aviation services program conducted at both CONUS and OCONUS locations. The ideal candidate possesses strong executive leadership skills, extensive experience in program integration, aviation operations support, and a proven ability to lead large multidisciplinary teams operating in austere, dynamic, and sometimes hostile environments.

Primary program management activities are headquartered at Patrick Air Force Base, Florida, with travel to multiple OCONUS locations as required by mission needs.

The Program Manager acts as a primary interface with U.S. Government stakeholders, oversees program performance across operations, maintenance, logistics, and training functions, and ensures compliance with all contractual, regulatory, and international requirements. The PM must be capable of rapid decision-making, effective risk management, and developing/implementing strategies that directly support INL/A’s mission of providing safe, secure, and responsive aviation support worldwide.

This position is contingent on an upcoming proposal.

What You Will Do

Provide full-spectrum program management oversight for all INL/A contract requirements including operations, aviation services, logistics, maintenance, engineering, training, safety, and quality assurance.
Serve as the principal point of contact with the Government Program Directorate, COR, GTMs, and associated U.S. Embassy Country Teams, ensuring timely communication, coordination, reporting, and issue resolution.
Direct all phases of program execution from initiation through completion, ensuring adherence to cost, schedule, and performance baselines while maintaining rigorous safety and quality standards.
Lead program review sessions, present cost/schedule/technical performance data, and oversee risk identification, mitigation, and mission planning in support of INL/A operations.
Coordinate across multiple contractors, subcontractors, and associate contractor agreements to achieve seamless integration of aviation operations, logistics, IT services, maintenance, and support activities.
Ensure program compliance with all applicable federal acquisition regulations, export controls (ITAR/EAR), aviation regulatory standards, and INL/A directives.
Oversee workforce planning, recruitment, and retention of U.S. Expatriate, TCN, and local-national personnel to support nationalization strategies and operational requirements.
Maintain oversight of safety programs, quality assurance processes, and internal controls to promote continuous improvement and prevent mishaps in high risk environments.
Manage program data accuracy and reporting requirements, ensuring all forms, records, and deliverables are produced on time and in accordance with contract and regulatory guidance.
Develop and implement strategic recommendations to improve lifecycle sustainment, operational efficiency, and fleet modernization in support of INL/A goals.
Represent the contractor in operational planning, coordination meetings, and interagency forums, ensuring alignment with INL/A mission objectives and foreign mission requirements.

What We Are Looking For

8 years relevant progressive experience with Bachelors in related field; 6 years relevant progressive experience with Masters in related field; or High School Diploma or equivalent and 12 years relevant progressive experience.
Minimum 10+ years leading complex mission operations or large-scale aviation programs.
Experience managing programs valued at $100M+.
Minimum 10 years of broad, in-depth senior management experience in business process development, organizational leadership, project/program management, process improvement, or change management.
Demonstrated expertise directing large, complex aviation or technical programs, including multi task, high complexity operations with diverse staff and subcontractors.
Proven ability to lead cross organizational teams, diagnose and correct organizational performance gaps, and manage large scale mission critical programs.
Experience conducting strategic and tactical planning, implementing change initiatives, and ensuring performance outcomes in demanding operational environments.

Demonstrated experience managing a multi-year schedule

Experience with Waterfall Project methodology
Experience applying Waterfall governance and procurement controls in conjunction with Agile solution delivery

About the role: Strategic Project Manager to lead the replacement of its legacy probation case management system. This role bridges technical infrastructure, legislative and policy compliance, and the daily experience of probation officers, judicial staff, and justice-involved individuals across Colorado's 23 judicial districts. The position will operate within a multi-level governance framework, supporting executive decision-making, managing stakeholder alignment, and facilitating issue escalation across business, technology, and judicial leadership.

Responsibilities

Strategic leadership and governance

Lead the full project lifecycle, from requirements and procurement through design, build, data migration, testing, statewide rollout, and decommissioning of ICON/JPOD.
Develop and maintain the master schedule, budget, scope baseline, and benefits realization plan.
Translate the Branch's strategic goals for probation into clear project objectives and measurable success criteria.

Vendor and procurement management

Support the solicitation, evaluation, and selection of a solution vendor under state procurement rules.
Hold vendors and internal teams accountable for quality, schedule, and cost.

Legislative and policy compliance

Track Colorado statutes, Chief Justice Directives, and probation standards affecting system requirements, and build them into the solution.
Coordinate with legal, policy, and research staff so the system supports required reporting, risk and needs assessments, and evidence-based practices.

Stakeholder engagement and change management

Engage chief probation officers, officers, supervisors, judges, court staff, and partner agencies across all 23 judicial districts, urban and rural alike.
Lead human-centered design activities, such as field observation, user testing, and feedback loops with frontline staff.
Direct organizational change management, training, communications, and go-live support.
Make sure the client-facing parts of the system are accessible, plain-language, and equitable for justice-involved individuals.

Risk, quality, and reporting

Identify, track, and mitigate risks and issues; escalate decisions promptly.
Plan cutover so probation supervision is never interrupted.
Report status, risks, and outcomes to leadership.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Project and program management: command of predictive, Agile, and hybrid methods, and the judgment to choose between them.
Systems thinking: ability to understand how technology, policy, operations, and people interact, and to see downstream effects of design choices.
Communication: clear, plain-language writing and speaking for audiences ranging from judges and legislators to frontline officers and vendors.
Facilitation and influence: ability to build consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, without direct authority.
Empathy for users: genuine interest in how probation officers and clients experience the system, and the discipline to design around their needs.
Analytical skills: ability to interpret data, evaluate trade-offs, and make sound decisions under uncertainty.
Integrity and discretion: sound handling of confidential criminal justice information and sensitive organizational matters.
Resilience: steady leadership through ambiguity, setbacks, and the pressures of a high-visibility public project.
Benefits orientation: understanding of business outcomes and the ability to support measurement of adoption and value realization objectives.
Governance and executive engagement: ability to operate within complex governance structures, prepare executive decision materials, facilitate escalations, and support leadership decision-making across multiple organizational levels.
Change management: ability to support organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and user adoption activities.

jobs.description:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

About the Role :

We are seeking a Senior Portfolio Program Manager to provide standing, exception-based orchestration across an assigned Research & Development (R&D) pillar. Reporting to the Head of Program Management, this individual contributor partners with Product and Engineering Pillar Leaders to maintain a connected view of portfolio commitments, dependencies, risks, capacity, readiness, and key decisions while improving delivery predictability and organizational effectiveness. Combining Agile coaching with portfolio program management, the role helps teams strengthen planning discipline, execution health, and continuous improvement while translating team-level insights into actionable portfolio visibility and leadership decision support.

The role also serves as a champion for AI-enabled Program Management, continuously identifying and introducing automation, emerging technologies, and workflow improvements that increase scalability, operational efficiency, and decision-making effectiveness. The Portfolio Program Manager coordinates, synthesizes, and escalates material exceptions across teams, product areas, pillars, and functions.

Accountability for product strategy, roadmap priorities, customer outcomes, engineering architecture, technical design, staffing, performance management, team execution, Scrum practices, backlog management, Jira hygiene, funding decisions, launch approvals, and risk acceptance remains with the appropriate Product, Engineering leaders. End-to-end ownership of strategic initiatives is assumed only when explicitly assigned.

Key Responsibilities :

Partner with Product and Engineering Pillar Leaders to establish and maintain portfolio baselines, including commitments, milestones, dependencies, ownership, readiness expectations, capacity assumptions, and success measures.
Maintain visibility into portfolio commitments and execution progress, surfacing material variances and coordinating appropriate change-management actions when scope, timeline, resource, or delivery commitments materially change.
Establish and continuously improve portfolio metrics, dashboards, reporting practices, automation, and AI-enabled workflows that strengthen portfolio visibility, decision-making, execution transparency, and operational efficiency.
Identify, evaluate, and introduce AI, automation, and emerging technologies that improve Program Management effectiveness, scalability, decision-making, and operational efficiency across the R&D pillar.
Partner with R&D Operating System teams to improve data quality, portfolio tooling, process standards, reporting, and adoption of portfolio management practices.
Establish and maintain visibility into cross-team and cross-pillar dependencies, ensuring ownership, impacts, required dates, and status are understood and tracked.
Coordinate dependency management across teams and pillars, facilitate alignment, resolution discussions, and escalate unresolved risks, impacts, and decisions through established governance forums.
Lead portfolio reviews focused on material changes, risks, dependencies, readiness gaps, capacity conflicts, and decisions requiring leadership attention.
Facilitate scaled planning, portfolio governance, and synchronization forums that improve alignment, transparency, and execution across the pillar.
Support quarterly planning cycles by validating commitments, dependencies, capacity assumptions, risks, and decision readiness across the pillar.
Synthesize portfolio information into decision-ready executive insights, including risks, dependencies, trade-offs, and recommendations, and ensure resulting decisions, escalations, and accountable follow-through are tracked through closure.
Coach Product and Engineering teams on Agile practices, planning discipline, delivery predictability, flow efficiency, and continuous improvement to strengthen execution effectiveness and delivery outcomes.
Identify work that may warrant dedicated Strategic Initiative Program Management support and provide evidence to support coverage decisions.
Coordinate with Strategic Initiative Program Managers to incorporate initiative health, dependencies, change impacts, and readiness into the pillar portfolio view.

Qualifications :

8+ years of experience in Portfolio Management, Program Management, Technical Program Management, Product Operations, or related roles within a SaaS or technology environment.
Experience leading Product and Engineering portfolios spanning multiple teams, product areas, or organizational units.
Experience establishing and leading portfolio governance frameworks, operating rhythms, quarterly planning processes, executive review forums, and reporting mechanisms that improve visibility, alignment, decision-making, and execution predictability.
Demonstrated success managing portfolio risk, dependencies, capacity constraints, competing priorities, and roadmap execution at scale.
Experience facilitating executive, leadership, and cross-functional governance forums that drive alignment, accountability, and decision-making.
Demonstrated success improving team effectiveness, delivery predictability, planning maturity, flow efficiency, and execution outcomes through Agile coaching, facilitation, and continuous improvement practices.
Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority, navigate ambiguity, clarify accountability, and drive alignment, decision-making, and follow-through across multiple stakeholders.
Experience identifying, evaluating, and implementing automation, AI-enabled workflows, and emerging technologies that improve portfolio visibility, operational efficiency, scalability, and decision-making effectiveness.
Strong analytical, facilitation, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into executive-ready insights and recommendations.
Working knowledge of Productboard, Jira, Confluence, dashboarding, and business intelligence platforms.
Agile coaching or Agile delivery certifications such as ICP-ACC, CSP, CSM, PSM, SAFe SPC, SAFe Agilist, or equivalent practical experience.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Success In This Role :

Trusted portfolio visibility enables informed leadership decisions.
Risks, dependencies, and changes to commitments are identified and addressed early.
Capacity and readiness issues are surfaced before they impact delivery.
Portfolio governance drives timely decisions and clear accountability.

jobs.description:
Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space—for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra's ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed.

About The Team

Mission Solutions - The Platforms

Mission Solutions builds on Umbra's expertise in remote sensing and spacecraft operations to engineer platforms purpose-built for U.S. and allied defense and intelligence missions. Whether it's a custom payload, a full-stack spacecraft, or the infrastructure behind an entire constellation, our team delivers secure, resilient systems tailored to exacting requirements and built on timelines that match the urgency of the mission.

If you want to work on cutting-edge space technology that's redefining what's possible in space platforms, you belong here at Umbra.

About The Job

As a Program Manager
, you will be responsible for delivering exceptional products, systems, services, and solutions that exceed customer expectations across cost, schedule, and technical performance. The position requires a strong understanding of how technical, financial, and organizational elements align to drive program success, including the development of structured roadmaps, schedules, and budgets that are actively managed throughout the program lifecycle.

The Program Manager will work closely with Umbra's product management team to define development scope and ensure execution aligns with the principles of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe). Success in this role depends on effective communication across both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including providing concise leadership updates and maintaining strong customer relationships. A deep understanding of Umbra's technologies enables informed oversight of technical progress and proactive management of risks and challenges.

In addition to program execution, you will contribute to business development activities, including proposals, RFI responses, customer engagement, and organic growth initiatives. The Program Manager also serves as a capture manager, leading capture strategy and proposal development for pursuits of varying size and complexity that align with Umbra's strategic campaigns.

This position is based on-site in either our Arlington, VA office or Reston, VA office.

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution: Take complete responsibility for the successful implementation (including cost, schedule, and technical aspects) of several ongoing contracts. Ensure monthly updates of financial results and forecasts. Deliver monthly status reports to facilitate Program Management Reviews.
Processes: Participate in the maturation of Umbra's Program Excellence Framework, which consists of documented procedures for initiating, executing, and concluding programs. Utilize insights and experiences gained from previous programs, while customizing them to align with Umbra's operational style, to establish streamlined processes for areas including financial management, risk management, contractual obligations, and performance monitoring.
Agile Development: Serve as the Business Owner for technologies associated with contracts. Collaborate with product management and system architects on engineering solutions. Engage actively in key Agile ceremonies, including PI planning.
Growth and Strategy: Take the lead in capture, developing winning proposals and creating compelling solutions. Create and implement growth strategies for existing and upcoming contracts. Act as the customer's advocate in product management to help shape company roadmaps based on their requirements.
All other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, business, or a related STEM or business field.
5+ years of relevant professional experience, including 3+ years of program management experience supporting U.S. Government contracts or programs within the aerospace and defense industry.
Experience working in a cleared environment within the past two years.
Demonstrated ability to manage technical development and/or R&D programs, including coordination of multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Strong understanding of product and technology development lifecycles.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams, customers, and senior leadership.

Desired Qualifications

Master's degree in engineering or a related STEM field.
8+ years of program management experience supporting U.S. Government contracts or programs within the aerospace and defense industry.
Active TS/SCI security clearance, with a read-in within the past two years.
Demonstrated ability to independently plan, lead, and execute complex programs, including building and coordinating high-performing teams.
Experience supporting or leading U.S. Government capture efforts, competitive proposals, and business development initiatives.
Direct experience managing space industry programs, including satellite development, integration, testing, and/or mission operations.
Experience supporting a diverse range of U.S. Government customers, including the Department of Defense (DoD), Intelligence Community (IC), and civil agencies.
Familiarity with remote sensing technologies, including Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), RF space payloads, and associated ground systems.
Understanding of systems engineering principles, processes, and system architectures.
Familiarity with program management and Agile frameworks, such as PMI, SAFe, or similar methodologies.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment, demonstrating initiative, adaptability, sound judgment, and comfort navigating ambiguity.

Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

Lead financial and business support for Diagnostic Imaging and Procedures, including operational and capital budget development, variance analysis, forecasting, and financial reporting in partnership with departmental leaders.
Manage contracts and purchasing activities, including Statements of Work (SOWs), Third-Party Agreements (TPAs), vendor contracts, and purchase orders (POs), ensuring compliance, fiscal stewardship, and alignment with organizational policies.
Oversee capital planning and management, supporting capital requests, business justifications, prioritization, tracking, and post-implementation financial review in collaboration with clinical, operational, and finance partners.
Develop proformas and light business plans for new services, programs, staffing, equipment, and operational changes, providing actionable financial analysis to support leadership decision-making.
Support provider staffing, FTE, and resource planning, including staffing assessments, financial modeling, and coordination of FTE and provider staffing requests.
Partner with leaders to design and maintain financial and operational planning tools, supporting budgetary, volume, staffing, and operational forecasting across Imaging and Procedures to include research and clinical operations.
Provide financial education and consultative support to departmental leaders, translating complex financial data into clear, practical insights to strengthen financial literacy and operational accountability.
Support vendor negotiations and grant activities, including financial evaluation of vendor proposals, cost containment initiatives, budgeting, tracking, and reporting for departmental grants and external funding.

Strong knowledge of healthcare financial operations, budgeting, and business planning
Experience with contracts, SOWs, TPAs, vendor management, and PO processes
Ability to analyze and interpret financial data and present insights clearly

Define and track delivery, adoption and risk-reduction measures to confirm intended benefits are realised.
Build trusted relationships with sponsors, business owners, technology leaders, risk teams and operational stakeholders across multiple regions and time zones.

Operational Management
