Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

As a Principal Data Analyst, you are a highly analytical, technically strong, forward-thinking problem solver who thrives on turning data into strategic insight and building modern decision products. You will play a pivotal role within the Decision Intelligence team, combining deep analytical expertise with hands-on technical skills to solve complex business problems using enterprise data, business intelligence, artificial intelligence (AI), and automation.

This is a hands-on technical role with significant visibility across the organization. You will work directly with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders while personally designing and building analytical solutions - ranging from enterprise semantic models and Power BI experiences to AI-powered applications and agents. Your work will directly influence strategic decisions and help evolve how the enterprise consumes data, insights, and AI.

What You'll Get To Do

Promote Data-Driven Decision-Making: Translate ambiguous business questions into analytical solutions that go beyond stated needs - proactively surfacing insights, root causes, opportunities, and recommended actions that guide executive strategy and operational excellence.
Build Modern Decision Products: Personally design and build analytical products ranging from scalable semantic models and advanced Power BI experiences to AI-powered analytical applications and agents. Select the appropriate interface and technology based on the business problem rather than defaulting to traditional dashboards.
Build AI-Powered Analytical Solutions: Design, prototype, build, and help productionize AI-enabled analytical applications and agents that combine enterprise data, semantic context, large language models (LLMs), APIs, and tools to answer business questions, generate insights, and automate analytical workflows.
Collaborate Across the Business: Partner with leaders in designated departments and other domains to define key metrics, interpret performance results, understand business context, and connect analytics and AI solutions to financial, operational, customer, and growth objectives.
Engineer Trusted Analytical Foundations: Build and maintain reliable data models, metric definitions, semantic models, and analytical logic. Troubleshoot data gaps and partner with data engineering and governance teams to strengthen data quality, lineage, consistency, and trust.
Apply Practical AI and Automation: Identify high-value opportunities for AI and automation, then move beyond ideation to working solutions. Apply techniques such as tool/function calling, structured outputs, retrieval and grounding, context engineering, and agentic workflows where they provide measurable business value.
Evaluate for Accuracy and Reliability: Develop practical approaches to test and monitor AI-enabled analytical solutions, including grounding, hallucination and accuracy testing, regression testing, observability, and human review. Understand when deterministic analytics, traditional machine learning, or an LLM-based approach is most appropriate.
Communicate with Confidence: Synthesize complex analyses and technical solutions into clear, compelling narratives and present actionable insights, tradeoffs, and recommendations to senior leadership.

Skills And Experience We Value

Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Economics, Business Analytics, or a related analytical field; Master's degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in data analytics, business intelligence, analytical engineering, data science, decision science, or related technical roles, preferably in an enterprise SaaS, technology, consulting, or complex business environment.
Strong SQL, data modeling, and analytical engineering skills, with hands-on experience building enterprise analytics solutions using platforms such as Power BI. Candidates should be comfortable working directly in Power BI when needed, including semantic models, DAX, performance optimization, advanced dashboards, and executive-facing analytical products.
Strong hands-on Python skills and comfort working with APIs, Git, JSON, testing and debugging, notebooks, and modern development workflows used to build analytical and AI-enabled solutions.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building AI/LLM applications beyond the use of AI productivity tools or commercial chat applications. Experience should include several of the following: agentic workflows, tool/function calling, structured outputs, retrieval/RAG, context engineering, prompt design, API integration, and evaluation frameworks.
Demonstrated track record of personally designing and building AI-enabled analytical products or agentic systems from prototype toward production. Candidates should be prepared to discuss architecture, implementation decisions, evaluation methods, failures, tradeoffs, and lessons learned from systems they personally built.
Strong understanding of semantic modeling, metric design, KPI frameworks, business definitions, data quality, lineage, and governance practices needed to provide trusted context to both enterprise reporting and AI-enabled analytical experiences.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical and technical approaches, identify root causes, quantify business impact, and determine when a problem is best solved with SQL or deterministic software, traditional analytics or machine learning, a BI experience, or an LLM/agentic solution.
Experience evaluating AI systems for accuracy, grounding, reliability, and business usefulness, including approaches such as test datasets, hallucination testing, regression testing, observability, human review, and appropriate controls for enterprise use.
Proven experience leading complex analytical or AI initiatives from concept through implementation with minimal oversight, including requirements definition, stakeholder alignment, hands-on development, testing, delivery, adoption, and ongoing optimization.
Experience partnering with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to define success metrics, interpret performance trends, and connect analytical and AI solutions to financial, operational, customer, and growth outcomes.
Exceptional communication, analytical reasoning, and business acumen, with the ability to synthesize complex data and technical concepts into clear narratives, evaluate tradeoffs, prioritize work based on business value, and influence decisions at senior levels.
High degree of intellectual curiosity, ownership, technical judgment, and attention to detail. We value demonstrated building experience over theoretical familiarity; candidates should be prepared to discuss systems they personally designed and implemented. Experience working in the Human Capital Management industry is preferred.

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Stay current with emerging application security threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive techniques

At Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, we are committed to paving the way for everyone to achieve their healthiest life. We are looking for dedicated and motivated individuals who share our vision of transforming healthcare. As a Blue Cross associate, you are joining a culture that is built on values of succeeding together, finding a better way, and doing the right thing. If you are ready to make a difference, join us.

The Impact You Will Have

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota is hiring a Program Manager, Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality. In this position, you’ll be responsible for the design, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing management of the Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality Program, supporting Medicare, Medicaid, ACA, and Commercial populations to optimize Blue Cross’s earned risk-adjusted revenue. The role serves as the subject matter expert for risk adjustment coding, partnering with leadership and cross-functional teams to develop and execute strategic initiatives, identify data trends, and implement performance improvement opportunities through collaboration with analytics and other key stakeholders. The incumbent ensures program strategies and operations meet evolving regulatory, market, provider, and member requirements while addressing complex business challenges and supporting organizational change. Acting as a liaison across multiple departments, the individual leads enterprise-wide initiatives, drives results within established timelines, and provides leadership and oversight to program management staff within the division. Working closely with the Director, this position supports the implementation of strategic initiatives, monitors project progress, and oversees team and vendor performance to ensure key objectives and deadlines are achieved. The role leads coding and audits review activities, including medical record reviews to support accurate risk adjustment revenue, compliance, audits of provider and vendor documentation to ensure accuracy and completeness, and operational readiness efforts for government audits related to risk adjustment programs.

What You’ll Do

Lead Medicare Advantage (MA) and ACA Risk Adjustment coding operations, including chart review programs, RADV and HRADV audit readiness, and coding validation activities to ensure accurate risk score capture, regulatory compliance, and revenue optimization. Expert in HCC and HHS risk adjustment methodology.
Manage and develop a team of certified coding professionals (CPCs), providing leadership, oversight, and coaching while driving coding accuracy, quality performance, and operational excellence.
Partner with providers, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver risk adjustment education, ensure vendor performance and compliance, and implement strategies that improve documentation quality and audit outcomes.

Drive the development and documentation of design, requirements and implementation required to support initiatives that align with strategic priorities.
Develop relationships and partner with key resources, both internal and external, to collaborate on the design and ensure all market, member, and provider considerations are factored into the design.
Drive business decision making process to ensure capabilities, systems and processes meet market expectations and that alternate approaches are vetted and explored.
Manage related ongoing program management work to understand what is needed to recommend strategy and solutions, while influencing and steering others to accomplish that strategy across multiple complex programs.
Ensure that appropriate metrics are chosen and that the appropriate measurement, data analysis and evaluation occur for each initiative.
Develop and continually update program or project plans, timelines and deliverables while coordinating multiple sub-processes to expand and/or improve complex programs.
Develop and implement a communication plan in conjunction with leadership and to support initiatives, including status and progress updates.
Stay abreast of changes in the rapidly evolving health care marketplace and in regulatory or quality‑measurement programs.
Performs additional responsibilities consistent with the scope and level of the role, as assigned.

Required Skills & Experience

5+ years of progressive project/program management experience, with 1+ staff, team lead or project lead experience.
Bachelor’s degree; in lieu of a degree, an additional two years of relevant experience beyond the qualifications listed above may be accepted.

Preferred Skills & Experience

Strong knowledge of CMS risk adjustment models (ACA and Medicare Advantage).
Experience with HCC coding, RADV audits, and/or chart review programs preferred.
CPC, CCS or CRC coding certification strongly preferred.
Experience developing or supporting provider education or training initiatives preferred.
Masters degree in related field.
Ability to communicate expectations and priorities clearly to team members, actively listen to resolve issues and remove barriers, and drive alignment across teams and stakeholders.
Ability to analyze department challenges, guide team decision-making, and collaborate across teams to drive resolution and next steps.
Ability to effectively organize team work, balance priorities across projects, and manage time and resources to ensure timely delivery and coordination.
Healthcare or managed care experience.
Experience managing complex projects which may involve multiple team members, task assignment, working with internal or external clients, managing teams and customer relationships, and managing project deliverables.
Experience in data-driven decision-making.
Process improvement (Lean / Six Sigma) experience.
Familiarity with PM tools & Microsoft analytics tools.

Hybrid

Anchored in Connection

Our hybrid approach is designed to balance flexibility with meaningful in-person connection and collaboration. We come together in the office two days each week – most teams designate at least one anchor day to ensure team interaction. These in-person moments foster relationships, creativity, and alignment. The rest of the week you are empowered to work remote.

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
📍 Oslo / Bergen / Bodø

💰 Salary: 800 000 - 1 000 000 NOK/year

🌍 Why this role matters

Aidn has become the market leader in the municipal healthcare sector in Norway, and municipalities across the country are now being onboarded to our platform. That gives us something few companies have: the chance to change how an entire sector understands and uses its own data.

Today, most municipalities lack accessible, trustworthy insight into their own operational and clinical data. At the same time, they are facing an aging population that will put more pressure on their services every year. Good decisions will matter more than ever, and good decisions need good data.

Aidn Analytics is core to what we offer, but we are still early in defining what it will become. Whoever takes this role will help shape it from the ground up, at a time when AI is changing what insight work even looks like.

🔧 What You’ll Be Working On

As our Data Analyst, you will help Aidn and the municipalities make better decisions. You will build data products as part of your everyday work, and at the same time help set the standard for how data products get built across Aidn.

Your core responsibilities will include:

Building and maintaining analytics: Build the reports, dashboards, self-service tools, and data exports that municipalities and teams at Aidn rely on every day, with conversational analytics as an emerging capability.
Define what we measure: Defining metrics and balanced quality and performance indicators for the municipalities as well as for Aidn internally.
Working with municipalities: Working directly with municipal leadership and staff to translate operational and strategic questions into data products, and following up until those products are actually used.
Strengthening data literacy: both at Aidn and in the municipalities, by developing capabilities and training that enable users to be self-served and create value from our data products.
Setting the standard for how data products get built, including improving the developer experience supported by AI. Enabling others to build according to our best practices.
Supporting product teams and helping them move towards distributed data ownership where they create data products within their domain for internal and external purposes
Contributing to platform work, tooling adoption and the shared developer experience for insights work, and embedding in product teams when they need hands-on support

🤝Who You Are

We hire for attitude as much as for aptitude. Curiosity, ownership, and a collaborative spirit matter more than ticking every box.

That said, you’ll thrive here if you:

3+ years of experience in a data analyst role or similar, with an analytical mindset and a good understanding of what it takes to succeed with analytics.
A strong analytical mindset, turning vague questions into answers that change decisions. You ask good questions and work in a structured way with data, while thinking creatively and pragmatically about how we meet user needs. This is one of the most important qualities we’re looking for.
Write SQL independently at an advanced level, and have experience with modern data platforms (such as Databricks or Snowflake) and related tooling (such as dbt).
Are comfortable at both ends of the data value chain: you can bring in and model a new data source yourself, and you can also run a session with non-technical stakeholders to help them use and understand the data
You actively use AI in your analytics work today, and are curious about how AI, automation and new ways of working can raise the quality, speed and impact of what we deliver with data.
Have excellent communication skills, and have experience working with non-technical users and translating their needs, questions, and problems into data products
Experience from a product organisation, working in cross-functional teams where data products are built, shipped, and continuously improved.
Have built data products that people actually use in decision-making, and improved them over time.
A delivery-oriented, pragmatic approach, and the ability to take ownership and work independently in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.
Fluent Norwegian (C1 level) for collaboration and testing with municipal users, and professional English for internal collaboration.

Our analytics stack is built on Databricks, dbt, and Metabase. Experience with dbt or a similar transformation tool is a plus, as is experience with a self-service reporting tool, some Python, Amplitude, or a background in healthtech, the public sector, or another regulated data environment. None of these are dealbreakers.

👋
The Team

You will join our Data & Analytics team, a cross-functional team established in 2026 with a data engineer, a UX designer, two developers (including a tech lead) and a product manager. The team owns the shared data platform, the analytics capabilities and the overall Aidn Analytics experience. We aim for domain teams to own their analytical content; we own the platform, the governance and the holistic experience for anyone using or building analytics.

The team operates as its own product area and works closely with several product teams and our Infrastructure team.

Problems we’re working on right now include:

How do we build a modern data platform from a blank slate, with no legacy to migrate away from, in a way that will genuinely serve Aidn and the municipalities for years to come?
How do we help municipal care leaders move towards insight-based decisions, at both the strategic and operational levels, before the aging population wave hits?
How can AI and agents make data more accessible and understandable, both internally at Aidn and directly for municipal users?
How do we onboard many of Norway’s municipalities and shape a shared direction for Aidn Analytics together with them?

💬 What Success Looks Like

After 3 months:

Ramped up on Aidn’s domain and data model, and has met key municipal users and product teams.
Has delivered a few data products end-to-end, working with increasing independence.
The first data products are in real use by real customers.

After 6 months:

Owns reporting and analysis for a defined product or domain area.
Known and trusted by power users in the municipalities, and the natural point of contact at Aidn for data products and insights in that area.
Helps the team drive adoption of our data tooling.

After 12 months:

Spots opportunities in the data and across Aidn, rather than just responding to requests.
Has helped shape how the team defines and tracks success metrics, with a visible change in Aidn’s maturity as a data-driven organisation.
Has made a visible contribution to municipalities’ adoption of self-service analytics.

💙 Why you’ll love working here

High trust, real ownership. You’ll join a team with the freedom to explore challenging problems and own the results.
Visible impact. Your work will directly affect how healthcare professionals and municipalities across Norway do their jobs every day.
No legacy. You'll join a newly established team with no legacy, and the freedom to build great Data and Analytics experiences for our product teams and municipalities.
AI as a core tool. You'll actively incorporate AI into your work — experimenting with agentic tools, automating parts of your workflow, and helping define what responsible AI use looks like in Data & Analytics.

🎁 Perks And Benefits

6 weeks vacation
Flexible working hours and location
Health & wellness benefit
Employee shares
Pension, insurance, and full pay during parental leave
A collaborative, ambitious, and caring team.

👀 Interested?

We don't ask for cover letters. Just upload your CV or share your LinkedIn profile, and tell us what sparked your interest in the role.

We value diverse perspectives and would love to hear what you could bring to the Data & Analytics team. We can’t wait to see your application!

👉 Application deadline: November 8th, 2026

Aidn is part of the
Kernel cooperation
, where we build technology for the next generation of welfare societies.
With financial backing in order, we are privileged to be a fully autonomous startup busy building our company from the ground up the way we see fit.

Aidn recognizes and celebrates diversity in all its forms, visible and non-visible in all areas of the work environment. We work to promote an anti-discriminatory environment where everyone feels safe and welcome.

Read our full Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging policy in our handbook here.

We are looking for a Data Analyst to join a public equities investment team pursuing a quantamental strategy across alternative data and fundamental research. The role is centered on sourcing, validating, and scaling differentiated datasets that can improve security selection and deepen our understanding of company-specific and industry-level inflections. You should be equally comfortable working with messy data, testing hypotheses rigorously, and framing outputs in an investment context.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain workflows to ingest, clean, map, and analyze large-scale structured and unstructured datasets
Evaluate alternative data for relevance, integrity, coverage, timeliness, and predictive power
Conduct signal testing and backtesting to determine whether a dataset adds value to the investment process
Work closely with the investment team to turn raw data into actionable views on revenue trends, KPIs, competitive dynamics, and inflection points
Use AI agents and automation to accelerate research, tool-building, and internal processes
Support basic 3-statement modeling and connect data findings to fundamental underwriting

Requirements

1–3 years of experience, ideally at an alternative data vendor in research, product, or analytics
Strong Python and SQL skills
Demonstrated interest in public markets investing and differentiated research
Ability to distinguish signal from noise and apply judgment, not just run analysis
High ownership, speed, and intellectual curiosity

Strong candidates may also come from backgrounds such as investment banking with self-taught coding, or legal, market research, or other analytical roles where they independently built scrapers, worked with data, and developed a genuine investing process. Experience with large-scale data analysis across very large datasets
Web scraping, entity resolution, or API-based data collection
Familiarity with signal evaluation, time-series analysis, or statistical testing
Understanding of company KPIs, operating metrics, and financial statements
Personal investing experience or clear evidence of market obsession

About The Company

Nanophase Technologies Corporation is a rapidly growing company recognized by Fast Company as one of its Most Innovative Beauty Companies for 2023. Through its Solésence Beauty Science business, the company partners with beauty brands to develop and manufacture products that promote skin health. Its work is guided by the belief that the future of sun care is the future of beauty. Nanophase brings together scientific innovation, product development, and manufacturing expertise to help advance solutions for the beauty and personal care market.

About The Role

The Market & Business Analyst, Corporate Strategy is a foundational role within the Strategy, Marketing, and Communications function. Reporting to the Executive Director of Strategy, Marketing & Communications, this analyst will provide data, insights, and recommendations that support enterprise strategy and the company’s long-term vision. The role combines market and competitive intelligence, business analytics, financial modeling, and trend forecasting to inform marketing, business development, innovation, and leadership decisions.

The analyst will contribute to annual and three-year planning by using macro- and micro-level analysis to assess growth opportunities and strategic initiatives. This is a full-time, salaried-exempt position with a hybrid schedule requiring at least three days onsite each week. The standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree is required; an MBA, preferably from a top-tier program, is preferred. Candidates should have three to five years of experience in market research, competitive intelligence, business analysis, or a related field. Experience in health, beauty, wellness, consumer products, or CPG markets is an advantage.

Successful candidates bring strong research, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to synthesize complex or ambiguous datasets into clear, actionable recommendations. Experience building and analyzing financial or business models is important, as is understanding how commercial activity affects revenue, margins, and the P&L. Proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, Tableau, Salesforce, and other business intelligence, research, or dashboard tools is expected. Candidates should communicate confidently and concisely, including when presenting well-reasoned recommendations to executive audiences. Curiosity, attention to detail, sound judgment, initiative, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are essential.

Responsibilities

Own recurring market, trend, and competitive intelligence, monitoring industry benchmarks, economic shifts, and emerging opportunities. Prepare weekly and monthly analysis covering the company and its brand partners, and respond to ad hoc research requests across business functions. Assess brand health and contribute insights for category strategy, innovation pipelines, audience personas, and customer journeys.

Conduct white-space, category, market, opportunity, persona, and trend assessments. Gather and integrate information from internal systems, external databases, primary research, and secondary sources to develop cohesive insights for marketing, sales, innovation, business development, and leadership teams. Build and maintain live dashboards, including in Tableau, and create repeatable tools and models for cross-functional use. Communicate findings through written reports, visualizations, graph models, and presentations. Partner with IT to improve data management and automate reporting processes. Support strategic planning and other related activities as assigned.

Benefits

This full-time, salaried-exempt position offers a hybrid work arrangement, with at least three onsite days per week, and the opportunity to contribute to company-wide strategy and growth. Compensation is determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and role level. Details about applicable compensation and benefits will be shared during the hiring process.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or perception, national origin, age, marital or parental status, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Job Title:
Interdisciplinary AI Project Manager
Job Status:
Full-time, 18-month term (with projected extension), grant-funded position 
Reports to:
Senior Manager of Standards
Location:
Fully Remote 
Salary Range:
$80,000 – $85,000 annually
The Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA) is a membership organization that supports and promotes the teaching of computer science, providing opportunities for PK-12 teachers and their students to better understand computer science and to more successfully prepare themselves to teach and learn. 

CSTA is looking for an experienced Project Manager who will lead the implementation of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative, a national effort to bring computer science and other disciplines together to define and teach AI literacy across PK–12 education
. The Project Manager will coordinate convenings of national subject-area associations, manage the development of interdisciplinary instructional resources with CS and non-CS educators, guide dissemination and professional development aligned to these resources, and work with contractors and external reviewers to ensure all project deliverables are met, and advocate for adoption of the project's outputs across the education community. 
Project Description AI literacy can't be the responsibility of computer science alone. Students encounter AI in every subject, and each discipline has a distinct role in helping them understand, use, and critically evaluate it. The purpose of the Collaborative is to define that shared responsibility and give educators the tools to act on it.
CSTA is convening national subject-area associations, including those representing mathematics, English language arts, science, world languages, and technology and engineering into a cross-subject collaborative. Through three convenings, the collaborative will produce an interdisciplinary AI Literacies Framework and a Division-of-Labor Map describing how responsibility for AI literacy is distributed across subject areas. Both will be publicly launched at the CSTA Annual Conference in July 2027.
Alongside this work, the Collaborative brings CS and non-CS educators together in collaborative workshops to develop, classroom-test, and refine interdisciplinary instructional resources that integrate foundational AI concepts with subjects such as math, ELA, and social studies. The resources are aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards and other disciplinary standards. Together, these efforts will shape how AI literacy is taught across disciplines in schools nationwide. 
Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesFramework Development (30%) Contribute to the planning and facilitation of three cross-disciplinary convenings
to create an interdisciplinary AI literacy framework and division of labor map.
Synthesize convening and project outcomes and recommendations and publish supporting materials in report(s)
, in close collaboration with a contracted Report Writer, a contracted Designer, CSTA staff, and external reviewers.

Interdisciplinary Resource Development (30%) Refine and manage processes to develop, publish, and disseminate interdisciplinary instructional resources aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Standards and other disciplinary standards (e.g., Next Generation Science Standards, Common Core State Standards for Mathematics/ELA).
Recruit
representatives for collaborative, interdisciplinary instructional resource development.
Plan and facilitate
interdisciplinary instructional resource development workshops.
Facilitate
the development of interdisciplinary professional learning opportunities.

Project Management and Dissemination (40%) Manage the successful implementation
of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative project. Success includes the development and publication of an interdisciplinary framework for AI education and division-of-labor map, and the development and publication of interdisciplinary lesson plans across several subject areas.
Maintain the public-facing display
of developed resources.
Coordinate with external reviewers
and other contractors
to ensure needed feedback and timely delivery of project deliverables.
Work closely with CSTA staff to create and manage reporting
to sponsor(s) and other key audiences, including developing cross-subject case studies. 
Guide dissemination
and professional development
(PD) efforts aligned with the project's interdisciplinary resources and outputs.
Present
externally on the project across multiple audiences at regular intervals (6–12 times per year, domestically and virtually), and advocate
for adoption of the framework, division of labor map, and interdisciplinary instructional resources.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience & Qualifications You will be successful in this role if you have:
Demonstrated strong project management and organizational skills, including workflow management, coordinating a variety of tasks simultaneously, and attention to detail
Superior critical thinking skills and judgment, with an ability to maintain a professional, upbeat attitude
Demonstrated partner management experience, working with external stakeholders and delivering quality customer service and ability to continuously improve methods and procedures
A bachelors or masters degree in education, instructional design, computer science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience
Experience with PK-12 curriculum development

Experience in planning and facilitating meetings with clear objectives, agendas, and collaborative structures
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially on virtual interfaces; comfort with speaking to groups and presenting information
Comfort with working in a remote environment; proficiency in working with technology – including but not limited to Google Workspace, videoconferencing (e.g., Zoom), project management software (e.g., Asana), and electronic communications (e.g., Slack)
Commitment to engaging in CSTA's efforts towards embracing diversity, being purposefully inclusive, and addressing anti-racism in CS education
The ability to travel up to 15% of the time (all travel costs are covered by CSTA)
The ability and willingness to shift work schedule to support or manage professional learning in afternoons, evenings, and weekends to accommodate teacher participants

Preferred Qualifications Experience teaching PK-12 computer science and/or AI literacy skills
Experience with interdisciplinary or cross-curricular teaching or curriculum design, particularly integrating computing into other subject areas
Experience working with national education organizations, coalitions, or multi-organization partnerships
Experience as a CSTA volunteer, committee member, chapter leader, or similar leadership role in an organization for PK-12 teachers

Position Terms This is a grant-funded position termed for 18-months. Position extension is planned but contingent on funding and approval by the CSTA Executive Director. CSTA is unable to sponsor employment visas. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a pre-employment background check and verification of eligibility to work in the United States.

Operating with significant autonomy, the Real Estate Program Manager manages large-scale initiatives through all phases of planning and execution, providing analytical insights, influencing key decisions, and ensuring successful project outcomes. The ideal candidate combines deep commercial real estate expertise with strong program management, business acumen, and the ability to influence outcomes across cross-functional teams without direct authority.

Lead real estate programs and strategic initiatives that support capacity growth, market expansion, portfolio optimization, and business objectives.

jobs.description:
Description

Fauna Robotics is looking for a Technical Program Manager to own quality for robot behavior and data collection. You will write and maintain the test suite that every release and every new policy goes through. That suite has two layers. The first is a core set of regression tests that confirms, every time, that the robot's locomotion, manipulation, mode transitions, and autonomy hand-offs still behave as expected. The second, and harder, layer goes looking for the subtle problems a routine pass will miss: failures that appear only in particular sequences of events, under particular loads, or in the interaction between the operator, the teleoperation stack, and the robot. You will run these tests yourself on experimental hardware, write clear and reproducible reports, and work with the engineering teams until each issue is understood and resolved.

You will also help keep the data we collect at a high quality through hands-on, on-site work with the robots: supporting benchmark collections, reviewing recorded episodes, and tracking data problems back to their root cause, whether that's the operator, the teleoperation stack, the robot, or the pipeline. As new collection tasks come out of research, you'll pilot them on hardware with the data scientists who designed them, validate the tools and methods they depend on, and say whether they're ready to run at scale. You'll be the go-to person for bringing new data collectors and QA team members up to speed on our teleoperation stack, our data collection management and ingestion tools, and the basics of finding, triaging, and reporting bugs.

Key job responsibilities

Own the release test suite for robot behavior and teleoperation. Write, maintain, and run test plans for updates to the teleoperation stack, internal and external software releases, and new robot policies.
Maintain a repeatable core regression suite that every change must pass, and extend it with deeper, adversarial test cases designed to surface subtle, intermittent, or interaction-dependent failures across the operator, the teleoperation stack, and the robot.
Run tests hands-on with experimental robots and in simulation. Write detailed, reproducible test reports and bug reports, and give clear go/no-go recommendations for each release and each new policy.
Track issues through to resolution with software, controls, hardware, and ML teams. Keep a record of known issues, how to reproduce them, and workarounds.
Support data quality through hands-on, on-robot testing: help run benchmark collections, review recordings against task requirements, flag problem episodes, and feed the failure patterns you find back to the teams that own the process and tooling.
Pilot new data collection tasks alongside data scientists and research engineers: translate research intent into an executable protocol, run the first sessions yourself, and report back on feasibility, throughput, and data quality.
Validate the data collection tools and methods behind each task before they're relied on at scale — define acceptance criteria, quantify failure modes, and make the go/no-go call. Iterate on task setups, scene design, and annotation schemas where the data doesn't hold up.
Onboard and mentor new data collectors and QA team members on our teleoperation stack, the data collection management system, the ingestion and annotation tools, and how to report bugs well.
Coordinate the day-to-day test and benchmark activities that data collectors take part in. Work with the data collection program manager, who owns the data collectors' work and priorities, to schedule robot time, sessions, and test coverage.
Assess the spaces and resources that testing and collection depend on — lab and home-like environments, robot availability, headsets and peripherals, fixtures and props — and flag what's missing before it becomes a bottleneck.

Keep test documentation, checklists, SOPs, and run books up to date as the robot, the app, and our policies change.

Work safely around experimental hardware, and hold the people you train to the same standard.

About The Team

Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won’t arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We’re changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We’re building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you’ll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It’s an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we’re interested in hearing from you.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical product or program management experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
3+ years of experience in quality assurance, test, or validation of hardware or hardware-plus-software products (robotics, consumer electronics, automotive, aerospace, XR, or similar), or in technical program management for such products
Experience writing and running structured test plans and SOPs, and producing detailed, reproducible test and bug reports with logs, timestamps, media, and system context
Experience working hands-on with physical robots or other experimental hardware in a lab or test environment, including diagnosing failures that span hardware, firmware, and software
Experience teleoperating robots, or extensive hands-on use of VR/XR headsets
Linux and command-line proficiency — able to run scripts and terminal tooling to drive, inspect, and debug hardware directly
Able to work in a VR headset for extended sessions (multiple hours at a time) and to work safely around experimental robots, which includes standing, moving, and occasionally lifting equipment
Able to lift up to 10 lbs and wear equipment weighing up to 30 lbs; continuous hand/eye coordination, fine manipulation, and kinesthetic awareness
Experience training, onboarding, or mentoring others on technical tools or processes
Ability to write technical documentation precise enough for an operator or support agent to follow without the author present

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Experience teleoperating robots with a Meta Quest 3 (or a similar VR teleoperation setup)
Experience with robot learning data collection, such as demonstration data, episode annotation, or dataset quality review
Experience validating robot control or learned policies on hardware before release
Experience leading QA across a hardware, firmware, and software product ecosystem, including fleet-level validation testing and catching performance regressions before release
Python scripting for hardware control; firmware flashing and diagnostic interfaces; electromechanical diagnostics (motors, sensors, thermal systems)
Experience using LLMs or AI coding tools to build simple internal tools such as dashboards, web UIs, or report generators to speed up QA work
Familiarity with issue trackers and test management tools, and with reading logs or telemetry to narrow down a failure
Experience coordinating the daily work of operators or test technicians without being their direct manager
Experience owning production incidents or executive escalations end-to-end in unfamiliar system architecture
Experience running observational research or usability studies and translating interaction data into product direction
Background in robotics, HRI, data operations, or games

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Champion Safety, Compliance, and Cross-Functional Alignment

Partner closely with internal engineering, construction, commercial, and operations teams to resolve technical challenges, maintain project momentum, and build long-run value.

Strong technical grounding in HV switchyards, substations, BESS integration, and large-scale power infrastructure, with proven ability to evaluate technical designs, equipment proposals, and change orders.

The Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA) is a membership organization that supports and promotes the teaching of computer science, providing opportunities for PK-12 teachers and their students to better understand computer science and to more successfully prepare themselves to teach and learn. 
CSTA is looking for an experienced Project Manager who will lead the implementation of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative, a national effort to bring computer science and other disciplines together to define and teach AI literacy across PK–12 education
. The Project Manager will coordinate convenings of national subject-area associations, manage the development of interdisciplinary instructional resources with CS and non-CS educators, guide dissemination and professional development aligned to these resources, and work with contractors and external reviewers to ensure all project deliverables are met, and advocate for adoption of the project's outputs across the education community. 
Project Description AI literacy can't be the responsibility of computer science alone. Students encounter AI in every subject, and each discipline has a distinct role in helping them understand, use, and critically evaluate it. The purpose of the Collaborative is to define that shared responsibility and give educators the tools to act on it.
CSTA is convening national subject-area associations, including those representing mathematics, English language arts, science, world languages, and technology and engineering into a cross-subject collaborative. Through three convenings, the collaborative will produce an interdisciplinary AI Literacies Framework and a Division-of-Labor Map describing how responsibility for AI literacy is distributed across subject areas. Both will be publicly launched at the CSTA Annual Conference in July 2027.
Alongside this work, the Collaborative brings CS and non-CS educators together in collaborative workshops to develop, classroom-test, and refine interdisciplinary instructional resources that integrate foundational AI concepts with subjects such as math, ELA, and social studies. The resources are aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards and other disciplinary standards. Together, these efforts will shape how AI literacy is taught across disciplines in schools nationwide. 
Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesFramework Development (30%) Contribute to the planning and facilitation of three cross-disciplinary convenings
to create an interdisciplinary AI literacy framework and division of labor map.

Synthesize convening and project outcomes and recommendations and publish supporting materials in report(s)
, in close collaboration with a contracted Report Writer, a contracted Designer, CSTA staff, and external reviewers.

Interdisciplinary Resource Development (30%) Refine and manage processes to develop, publish, and disseminate interdisciplinary instructional resources aligned to the 2026 CSTA PK–12 Standards and other disciplinary standards (e.g., Next Generation Science Standards, Common Core State Standards for Mathematics/ELA).

Recruit
representatives for collaborative, interdisciplinary instructional resource development.

Plan and facilitate
interdisciplinary instructional resource development workshops.

Facilitate
the development of interdisciplinary professional learning opportunities.

Project Management and Dissemination (40%) Manage the successful implementation
of the Cross Subject AI Collaborative project. Success includes the development and publication of an interdisciplinary framework for AI education and division-of-labor map, and the development and publication of interdisciplinary lesson plans across several subject areas.

Maintain the public-facing display
of developed resources.

Coordinate with external reviewers
and other contractors
to ensure needed feedback and timely delivery of project deliverables.

Work closely with CSTA staff to create and manage reporting
to sponsor(s) and other key audiences, including developing cross-subject case studies. 

Guide dissemination
and professional development
(PD) efforts aligned with the project's interdisciplinary resources and outputs.

Present
externally on the project across multiple audiences at regular intervals (6–12 times per year, domestically and virtually), and advocate
for adoption of the framework, division of labor map, and interdisciplinary instructional resources.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Demonstrated strong project management and organizational skills, including workflow management, coordinating a variety of tasks simultaneously, and attention to detail

Superior critical thinking skills and judgment, with an ability to maintain a professional, upbeat attitude

A bachelors or masters degree in education, instructional design, computer science, or related field, or equivalent practical experience

Familiarity with AI in PK-12 education, including foundational AI concepts and current AI literacy efforts

Experience in planning and facilitating meetings with clear objectives, agendas, and collaborative structures

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, especially on virtual interfaces; comfort with speaking to groups and presenting information

Comfort with working in a remote environment; proficiency in working with technology – including but not limited to Google Workspace, videoconferencing (e.g., Zoom), project management software (e.g., Asana), and electronic communications (e.g., Slack)

Commitment to engaging in CSTA's efforts towards embracing diversity, being purposefully inclusive, and addressing anti-racism in CS education

The ability and willingness to shift work schedule to support or manage professional learning in afternoons, evenings, and weekends to accommodate teacher participants

Preferred Qualifications Experience teaching PK-12 computer science and/or AI literacy skills

Experience as a CSTA volunteer, committee member, chapter leader, or similar leadership role in an organization for PK-12 teachers

Position Terms This is a grant-funded position termed for 18-months. Position extension is planned but contingent on funding and approval by the CSTA Executive Director. CSTA is unable to sponsor employment visas. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a pre-employment background check and verification of eligibility to work in the United States.

new_jobs.description:
Full-time Description

About Us

At Kroll Konstruction, we specialize in delivering complex projects with a focus on safety-first culture, quality, and collaboration. We are committed to the values of service, accountability, and doing whatever it takes to get the job done right.

Overview

The Project Manager role oversees commercial construction from setup to closeout, ensuring projects meet deadlines, stay within budget, and adhere to the highest safety and quality standards. This role requires strong leadership skills, excellent communication, and a hands-on approach to coordinating site activities, managing subcontractors, and upholding compliance with project requirements.

Requirements

Responsibilities:

Budget & Compliance Oversight

Collaborate with Accounting and Senior Leadership to maintain accurate reporting on budget performance and financial forecasts.
Develop, manage, and maintain project budgets from pre-construction through closeout, ensuring all expenditures align with approved costs and contractual limits.
Review and approve subcontractor/vendor invoices, change orders, and purchase requests to ensure cost accuracy and adherence to budget limits.
Identify and reconcile variances between planned and actual costs, taking prompt corrective action to maintain budget.
Ensure project compliance with applicable codes, regulations, safety standards, and company policies.

Contract Management

Review prime contracts, subcontracts, and purchase orders to confirm scope, schedule, and terms are properly executed and communicated.
Lead negotiations of subcontractor agreements and change orders in collaboration with Senior Leadership and relevant teams.
Monitor and enforce contract compliance, ensuring all parties meet deliverables, insurance requirements, and performance obligations.
Manage project documentation, including RFIs, submittals, and contract correspondence, ensuring traceability and timely resolution.
Oversee project closeout documentation, including warranties, support with lien waivers, and final payment approvals.

Scheduling & Project Oversight

Develop and maintain the project schedule in coordination with the superintendent, subcontractors, and Owners, ensuring milestones are met.
Identify potential delays or resource conflicts and implement mitigation strategies immediately with Senior Leadership to maintain on-time delivery.
Lead weekly coordination meetings with field and office teams to review progress, resolve issues, and forecast upcoming activities.
Monitor quality, safety, and performance in collaboration with Operations teams.
Ensure all work aligns with project specifications, drawings, and company standards for workmanship and professionalism.

Metrics & Reporting

Track and report key project metrics, including budget performance, schedule adherence, safety incidents, and quality control findings.
Prepare and present regular project status updates to relevant stakeholders.
Analyze performance data, identify trends, and recommend process improvements for future projects (Lessons Learned).
Maintain accurate documentation within project management platforms (e.g., RedTeam, BIM 360, etc.) to ensure transparency and accountability.

Subcontractor Management

Conduct pre-construction and weekly coordination meetings with Owners, Superintendents, and Leadership to align expectations.
Foster strong partnerships, escalating performance or contractual issues to Senior Leadership when necessary, to ensure collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Evaluate and oversee subcontractor performance, ensuring quality, safety-first culture, and schedule compliance.
Verify scope completion and assist with the approval of progress billings and retainage release.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent field experience.
OSHA 30 certification required; PMP certification preferred.
Advanced knowledge of construction contracts and project management practices, and regulatory requirements.
5+ years of demonstrated experience in commercial construction management, preferably with a general contractor, from bid to closeout.

Technical & Leadership Skills:

Proficiency with online project management or scheduling tools (RedTeam, Bluebeam, MS Project).
Skilled in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
Ability to partner cross-functionally to ensure contract-aligned scheduling, budgeting, and subcontractor coordination.
Experience managing design-build or fast-track projects.
Strong understanding of job cost tracking and forecasting principles.
Ability to analyze data, interpret reports, and identify cost or scheduling trends.
Leadership style rooted in accountability, collaboration, and safety-first culture.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Field personnel on construction project teams should expect 60-hour workweeks, with a minimum of 5 days a week and 8 hours per day, including weekends. Travel home is typically every week, but can shift to every third week depending on project needs. During the final month and a half of a project, it's common to remain on-site and take extra time off after completion.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.

Fine motor skills: Regular use of hands for tasks like typing, using a mouse, and handling documents.
Repetitive motions: Frequent reaching and arm movements, particularly when using the phone and during meetings.
Occasional lifting: The ability to lift up to 25 pounds may be required occasionally, but it's not a primary job function.

Kroll Konstruction Offers

100% company-paid premium medical, dental, vision, life ($50,000), AD&D ($50,000), and long-term disability insurance for our employees.
10 Paid Personal Days Off (PTO) and 8 Paid Holidays.
Discretionary Performance Bonus: Up to 10% of base salary, contingent upon company profitability and at the company's sole discretion.

Important Details:

This is a hybrid travel position requiring 100% travel availability based on project assignments.
Project Managers are expected to travel nationwide to active job sites, with a minimum of one site visit per week. Additional travel may be required based on project needs, project milestones, incident response, or strategic business initiatives.
When not assigned to a project site, work may be performed remotely from a home office, from one of our office locations, or from another approved work location.
Candidates must be willing and able to travel extensively, including overnight travel, as required to support project execution.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The Project Manager directs project staff and manages subcontractors to ensure effective coordination, strong performance, and adherence to safety and quality expectations.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Activities, duties, or responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Third-Party Recruiters

Kroll Konstruction does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies or search firms. Agencies should not contact hiring managers or other employees directly. All recruiting inquiries must be directed to the Human Resources Department. Resumes submitted without a current, signed vendor agreement will be considered the property of Kroll Konstruction, and no placement fee will be paid.

Salary Description $85,000.00- $115,000

Reports to: VP of Commercial Operations

Company Summary

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.

Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.

Backed by deep engineering expertise and large-scale manufacturing capability, Stellar Energy helps customers deploy critical infrastructure faster and with confidence.

Summary Objective

The Program Manager is responsible for leading the successful execution and coordination of complex customer (hyperscalers) programs involving multiple manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and cross-functional teams. This role will lead the coordination between Project Management, Product Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Scheduling, Supply Chain, Logistics, and Aftermarket Services to ensure Customer’s projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with customer expectations. The Program Manager drives financial performance, communication, manages project risks, improves operational processes, and ensures alignment across internal stakeholders while supporting Stellar Energy's commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction.

Essential Functions

Lead the on budget and on schedule execution and coordination of complex customer programs involving multiple manufacturing locations, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
Manage customer relationship throughout the project execution lifecycle, maintaining a clear understanding of project scope, schedules, technical requirements, and customer expectations.
Coordinate cross-functional teams including Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Scheduling, Logistics, Procurement, Project Management, and Aftermarket Services to ensure project milestones and deliverables are achieved.
Develop and maintain project execution plans while monitoring progress against established schedules, internal financial goals, and customer commitments. Identify financial and schedule project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and proactively resolve issues impacting project execution or customer delivery.
Collaborate with Aftermarket and Service organizations to ensure service requirements are aligned with customer needs. Establish standardized work processes that improve coordination across manufacturing locations and support consistent project execution.
Drive communication across internal stakeholders by facilitating project meetings, providing status updates, and escalating issues when necessary.
Monitor project performance metrics and recommend process improvements that enhance execution efficiency and customer satisfaction.
Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on project coordination, supply chain integration, and operational excellence.
Build strong working relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal business partners to ensure successful project outcomes.

Program and Project Management Cross-Functional Leadership Manufacturing Operations

Organizational and Planning Skills
Problem Solving and Decision Making
Communication and Presentation Skills
Time Management
Stakeholder Management
Continuous Improvement Mindset

Work Location

Work Environment
Most work is performed in an office environment with regular interaction with manufacturing operations, engineering teams, and project personnel. Occasional visits to fabrication facilities, distribution centers, customer sites, and supplier locations may be required.

Physical Demands

Description

We're seeking an experienced Sr. Technical Program Manager to lead the onboarding and stabilization of new internal customers into our manufacturing organization. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing operations, supply chain, and quality — driving the full lifecycle from initial customer engagement through pilot production, process validation, and steady-state handoff.

You will own the end-to-end program for bringing new products and programs into our manufacturing facility, building repeatable onboarding frameworks that scale as our customer base grows. This is a unique opportunity to shape how a growing internal manufacturing organization operates — establishing the mechanisms, processes, and cross-functional coordination that turn first-article builds into reliable production lines.

Key job responsibilities

Own the new customer onboarding lifecycle: from initial scoping and requirements gathering through pilot builds, process validation, acceptance testing, and transition to steady-state production
Define and manage the pilot manufacturing program (mission, vision, tenets, success criteria) with clear milestones, owners, and exit criteria for each onboarding phase
Translate ambiguous product requirements and engineering designs into structured manufacturing readiness plans — identifying tooling, fixturing, process, staffing, and facility needs before production starts
Drive cross-functional alignment between product engineering, manufacturing engineering, quality, supply chain, warehouse, and operations teams to ensure critical paths are identified and tackled effectively
Build and own the onboarding playbook: standardized gates, checklists, and readiness reviews (Design for Manufacturing reviews, First Article Inspections, Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, production trial runs) that each new program passes through
Identify risks and dependencies early — including supply chain readiness, BOM maturity, tooling lead times, workforce training gaps, and facility constraints — escalate with data, and drive resolution before they become roadblocks
Build and maintain mechanisms (reviews, dashboards, status cadences, clear-to-build tracking) that give leadership visibility into onboarding pipeline health without creating drag on production teams
Manage the manufacturing roadmap in partnership with engineering and operations leadership: sequence new program onboards against facility capacity, workforce availability, and existing production commitments
Drive continuous improvement of the onboarding process itself — capture lessons learned from each pilot, quantify cycle time and first-pass yield metrics, and implement changes that reduce time-to-stable-production for subsequent customers
Coordinate across organizations to unblock teams, resolve competing priorities between active production and new program introduction, and negotiate tradeoffs (time vs. quality vs. scope)
Partner with quality engineering to ensure new programs meet acceptance criteria and that manufacturing processes are validated (PPAP, APQP, or equivalent frameworks) before volume ramp
Oversee gaps between teams, processes, and systems — proactively reduce exposure to classic failure modes: requirements not sufficiently understood, ineffective cross-team collaboration, insufficient testing, unclear ownership boundaries between customer engineering and manufacturing
Write effective narratives and present program status, risks, and tradeoff recommendations to Directors and VPs
Mentor and develop junior TPMs and cross-functional team members; provide constructive feedback across engineering, manufacturing, and program management disciplines

Basic Qualifications

7+ years of technical program management experience
5+ years of experience working directly with engineering and/or manufacturing teams
3+ years of experience in manufacturing, new product introduction (NPI), or pilot production environments
Experience managing programs across multiple concurrent workstreams with competing priorities

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to support the growth of the world's most innovative HealthCare data platform. InterSystems HealthShare is the engine behind some of the world's most critical health applications. We are the platform technology that empowers mission-critical solutions across health plans, providers, and public sector.

About The Role

This is a founding Technical Program Manager role for HealthShare. You will report to the Head of Product and stand up the TPM function for the platform, defining how it works from the ground up. You will own the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Quality Development, and the Release Team: the dependencies between them, the handoffs where one team's work becomes another's, and the readiness of the releases that span all four.

This is a role for someone who has built this foundational function before and understands the distinction that makes it work. Engineering owns delivery on its teams. Quality owns quality. The Release Team owns the release. The TPM owns the seams between them, the cross-team dependency graph, and the standard for how work is tracked and made visible, without taking on the work that belongs to those teams or drifting into collecting status on their behalf.

If you are energized by defining an operating model rather than inheriting one, and by making a fast-moving, technically deep organization legible to itself without slowing it down, this role is built for you.

What You'll Own

The seams between Product, Engineering, Quality Development, and the Release Team. Name the handoffs, assign an owner on each side, define what passes across each boundary, and set the escalation path for when something breaks, before the release that tests it.
The cross-team dependency graph. Maintain an explicit, current picture of what depends on what across teams, so the organization can make deliberate decisions about sequencing and risk instead of discovering a major dependency the week it blocks a release.
Launch and release readiness for cross-functional work that spans multiple teams. Know, before a date is committed, whether the engineering work, the quality gates, the release steps, and the downstream communication are going to converge.
The tracking standard in Jira and Confluence. Define how work is structured and made visible, so program state is readable directly, without a status meeting. Make the compliant path the easy path so teams follow it because it helps them, not because they are told to.
Risk identification and communication across the platform. Surface the cross-team risks the individual teams are too close to see and get them in front of the right people early, using Teams and the tools the organization already operates.
Program-level visibility for leadership. Give the Head of Product and senior stakeholders a legible read on program health that is a byproduct of how teams already work, not a separate reporting tax layered on top of them.

What We're Looking For

10+ years in technical program management or a closely related discipline, including experience standing up or scaling a program-management function, not only running programs within an existing one.
Strong technical fluency. You do not need to write production code, but you should read a system well enough to find the real risk in a plan and hold your own with senior engineers on dependencies and architecture.
Experience delivering managed services and cloud services, and comfort with the operational realities of both.
A clear, demonstrated point of view on the difference between technical program management and a PMO, and on why performing hygiene work on behalf of teams is a failure mode rather than a service.
A track record of building cross-functional processes and interfaces that held up under real delivery pressure, spanning engineering and the teams downstream of it.
Experience defining a tracking standard that many teams run on, in Jira, Confluence, or equivalent tooling.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You can make a technical program legible to an engineer and to an executive in the same day, and you can hold a position through clarity and judgment rather than positional authority.
Strong organizational instincts and attention to detail, balanced by the judgment to add the minimum process a problem actually requires.

Tools You'll Work With

Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft productivity applications.

InterSystems, a creative data technology provider, delivers a unified foundation for next-generation applications for healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and supply chain customers in more than 80 countries. Our data platforms solve interoperability, speed, and scalability problems for large organizations around the globe to unlock the power of data and allow people to perceive data in imaginative ways. Plan cutover so probation supervision is never interrupted.
Report status, risks, and outcomes to leadership.

new_jobs.description:
Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space—for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra's ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed.

About The Team

Mission Solutions - The Platforms

Mission Solutions builds on Umbra's expertise in remote sensing and spacecraft operations to engineer platforms purpose-built for U.S. and allied defense and intelligence missions. Whether it's a custom payload, a full-stack spacecraft, or the infrastructure behind an entire constellation, our team delivers secure, resilient systems tailored to exacting requirements and built on timelines that match the urgency of the mission.

If you want to work on cutting-edge space technology that's redefining what's possible in space platforms, you belong here at Umbra.

About The Job

As a Program Manager
, you will be responsible for delivering exceptional products, systems, services, and solutions that exceed customer expectations across cost, schedule, and technical performance. The position requires a strong understanding of how technical, financial, and organizational elements align to drive program success, including the development of structured roadmaps, schedules, and budgets that are actively managed throughout the program lifecycle.

The Program Manager will work closely with Umbra's product management team to define development scope and ensure execution aligns with the principles of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe). Success in this role depends on effective communication across both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including providing concise leadership updates and maintaining strong customer relationships. A deep understanding of Umbra's technologies enables informed oversight of technical progress and proactive management of risks and challenges.

In addition to program execution, you will contribute to business development activities, including proposals, RFI responses, customer engagement, and organic growth initiatives. The Program Manager also serves as a capture manager, leading capture strategy and proposal development for pursuits of varying size and complexity that align with Umbra's strategic campaigns.

This position is based on-site in either our Arlington, VA office or Reston, VA office.

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution: Take complete responsibility for the successful implementation (including cost, schedule, and technical aspects) of several ongoing contracts. Ensure monthly updates of financial results and forecasts. Deliver monthly status reports to facilitate Program Management Reviews.
Processes: Participate in the maturation of Umbra's Program Excellence Framework, which consists of documented procedures for initiating, executing, and concluding programs. Utilize insights and experiences gained from previous programs, while customizing them to align with Umbra's operational style, to establish streamlined processes for areas including financial management, risk management, contractual obligations, and performance monitoring.
Agile Development: Serve as the Business Owner for technologies associated with contracts. Collaborate with product management and system architects on engineering solutions. Engage actively in key Agile ceremonies, including PI planning.
Growth and Strategy: Take the lead in capture, developing winning proposals and creating compelling solutions. Create and implement growth strategies for existing and upcoming contracts. Act as the customer's advocate in product management to help shape company roadmaps based on their requirements.
All other duties as assigned.
